- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpAlertDialog]` is `KpAlertDialog`. `exportAs: "kpDialog"`. `kpAlertDialog`, on any element or on `<ng-container>`: a dialog that asks for an answer. It is always modal and a press outside it never closes it, so it takes neither `[modal]` nor `[disablePointerDismissal]`. Its parts are a dialog's (`kpDialogTrigger`, `kpDialogPopup` …), which find it as their root. Its props are above.
- `[kpDialogTrigger]` is `KpDialogTrigger`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).
- `[kpDialogPortal]` is `KpDialogPortal`. Structural: written `*kpDialogPortal`. `<ng-template kpDialogPortal>` or `*kpDialogPortal`: its content at the end of the page while open.
- `[kpDialogBackdrop]` is `KpDialogBackdrop`.
- `[kpDialogViewport]` is `KpDialogViewport`. What a long dialog scrolls in, around its popup: it may be left out. A dialog's and an alert dialog's; a drawer lies at an edge of the page and has none.
- `[kpDialogPopup]` is `KpDialogPopup`.
- `[kpDialogTitle]` is `KpDialogTitle`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `[kpDialogDescription]` is `KpDialogDescription`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `[kpDialogClose]` is `KpDialogClose`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
- close: A button that closes the dialog.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `title` and `description`.

### Autocomplete

```
import { KpCombobox, KpComboboxInput, KpComboboxTrigger, KpComboboxClear, KpComboboxPortal, KpComboboxPositioner, KpComboboxPopup, KpComboboxList, KpComboboxCollection, KpComboboxGroup, KpComboboxGroupLabel, KpComboboxSeparator, KpComboboxItem, KpComboboxEmpty, KpComboboxStatus } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpAutocomplete]`, `input[kpComboboxInput]`, `[kpComboboxTrigger]`, `[kpComboboxClear]`, `[kpComboboxPortal]`, `[kpComboboxPositioner]`, `[kpComboboxPopup]`, `[kpComboboxList]`, `[kpComboboxCollection]`, `[kpComboboxGroup]`, `[kpComboboxGroupLabel]`, `[kpComboboxSeparator]`, `[kpComboboxItem]`, `[kpComboboxEmpty]`, `[kpComboboxStatus]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpAutocomplete
  input[kpComboboxInput]
  kpComboboxTrigger
  *kpComboboxPortal
    kpComboboxPositioner
      kpComboboxPopup
        kpComboboxList (optional)
          *kpComboboxCollection (optional)
            kpComboboxItem (repeated, as above)
            kpComboboxGroup (optional, repeated, as above)
          kpComboboxGroup (optional, repeated)
            *kpComboboxCollection (optional, as above)
            kpComboboxItem (repeated)
            kpComboboxGroupLabel
          kpComboboxSeparator (repeated)
        *kpComboboxCollection (optional, as above)
        *kpComboboxEmpty
        kpComboboxStatus (optional)
  kpComboboxPopup (as above)
  kpComboboxStatus (optional, as above)
  *kpComboboxClear
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: (Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null)`: With `[multiple]="true"`, the chosen values.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null>`: The text it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `[(inputValue)]: string`: What the input says, `[(inputValue)]`. With `kpAutocomplete` the text is `[(value)]`.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once.
- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Its value can be read and not changed: the list still opens and can be gone through, but no press and no Enter chooses, nothing typed is taken, and its clear and chip buttons do nothing. Its value is still submitted.
- `name?: string`: The input's name in the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[] | readonly ComboboxGroupData<Value>[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The values with their labels: a list of them, groups of them (`{ value, items }`), or the labels by value. With a `*kpComboboxCollection` it is the list itself: the combobox filters it, and the collection draws what is left.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed; `null` shows every item.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `multiple?: Multiple`: Several values, each shown as a chip: `value` and `valueChanged` then hold a list. Bound to `true` (`[multiple]="true"`), it types them so. The bare attribute, or a bound boolean, works the same, and then `value` takes either and `valueChanged` is typed as one value: Angular's compiler gives a type parameter it cannot infer `any`, so only a literal `true` says it.
- `inline?: boolean`: The list is always in the page, with no popup: a command palette.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page: each item is then given its `index`.
- `presentation?: Presentation`: How the list opens: `"sheet"` from the bottom edge, modal, with a backdrop, the input then in the popup; `"auto"` a sheet on a narrow touch screen. Default `"popup"`.
- `sheetBelow?: number`: With `presentation="auto"`: the viewport's width under which a coarse pointer opens a sheet. Default 640.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: The first item shown for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter chooses it. Off by default.
- `itemToStringLabel?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the input shows for one, and what is filtered.
- `itemToStringValue?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the form is sent for one.
- `mode?: "list" | "both" | "inline" | "none"`: With `kpAutocomplete`: `"none"` shows the suggestions as the caller draws them; `"both"` and `"inline"` write the rest of the first that begins with what is typed into the input.
- `openOnInputClick?: boolean`: With `kpAutocomplete`: a press on the input opens the list.
- `(valueChanged): { value: true extends Multiple ? (false extends Multiple ? Value | null : Value[]) : Value | null details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the text is about to change, typed or chosen: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(inputValueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the input's text is about to change; `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpAutocomplete]` is `KpCombobox`. `exportAs: "kpCombobox"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown, Multiple extends boolean = false>`. `kpAutocomplete` is a combobox whose text is the value: `[(value)]` is the text, and the list only suggests. Its parts are the combobox's directives. Its props are above.
- `input[kpComboboxInput]` is `KpComboboxInput`. `<input kpComboboxInput>`: what is typed filters the list, which is placed against it.
- `[kpComboboxTrigger]` is `KpComboboxTrigger`.
- `[kpComboboxClear]` is `KpComboboxClear`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxClear`. `<button *kpComboboxClear>`: empties the input and the value; in the page while there is something to clear.
- `[kpComboboxPortal]` is `KpComboboxPortal`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpComboboxPositioner]` is `KpComboboxPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpComboboxPopup]` is `KpComboboxPopup`.
- `[kpComboboxList]` is `KpComboboxList`. The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
- `[kpComboboxCollection]` is `KpComboboxCollection`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxCollection`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `ComboboxEntry`. `<ng-container *kpComboboxCollection="let entry">` draws the list from the root's `items`: once for each item left for what was typed, or for each group that has items left. With `of` (`*kpComboboxCollection="let item; of: group"`), for each of that group's items left. The root then filters, and no item hides itself.
    - `of?: ComboboxEntry`: Written after the directive's value: `*kpComboboxCollection="…; of: …"`. A group the root's `items` gave: its items left are then what is drawn.
- `[kpComboboxGroup]` is `KpComboboxGroup`. Items that belong together, named by their `kpComboboxGroupLabel`. Hidden while none is shown.
- `[kpComboboxGroupLabel]` is `KpComboboxGroupLabel`. Names the group it is in. With no group around it, it is plain text.
- `[kpComboboxSeparator]` is `KpComboboxSeparator`. A line between groups.
- `[kpComboboxItem]` is `KpComboboxItem`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the combobox's value is while this item is chosen.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered and what the input shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
- `[kpComboboxEmpty]` is `KpComboboxEmpty`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxEmpty`. `<div *kpComboboxEmpty>`: in the page while no item is shown for what was typed.
- `[kpComboboxStatus]` is `KpComboboxStatus`. Says how the list stands ("3 results", "Loading") to software that reads the page, as its text changes. Keep it in the page and change what it holds: inside the popup, or beside the input.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input: its text is the value, and what is typed asks for suggestions.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry. As a sheet it is not placed, and carries none.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list. As a sheet, a design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: As a sheet, once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One suggestion: chosen, its text is written into the input.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value. It is in the page while there is something to clear (the text, for an autocomplete; else what is chosen), and through its exit; `keepMounted` keeps it there.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is something to clear.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `groupLabel`, `separator`, `empty` and `status`.

### Autosize

```
import { KpAutosizeTextarea } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `textarea[kpAutosizeTextarea]`.

Anatomy:

```
textarea[kpAutosizeTextarea]
```

Each part, and its own props:

- `textarea[kpAutosizeTextarea]` is `KpAutosizeTextarea`. `exportAs: "kpAutosizeTextarea"`. `<textarea kpAutosizeTextarea>`: as tall as its text.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `textarea`.

### Avatar

```
import { KpAvatar, KpAvatarImage, KpAvatarFallback } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpAvatar]`, `[kpAvatarImage]`, `[kpAvatarFallback]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpAvatar
  *kpAvatarImage (or kpAvatarImage as an attribute)
  *kpAvatarFallback
```

Props of its root:

- `(loadingStatusChanged): ImageStatus`: Each time the picture's loading status changes: `loading` once it has an address, then `loaded` or `error`; `idle` again when its address is taken away. Base UI's `onLoadingStatusChange`; the root says the same in `data-image-loading-status`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpAvatar]` is `KpAvatar`. `exportAs: "kpAvatar"`. `<span kpAvatar>`: the frame. `(loadingStatusChanged)` hears its picture's loading, in either of the image's forms (a structural directive's own outputs cannot be bound from its element). Its props are above.
- `[kpAvatarImage]` is `KpAvatarImage`. Structural or not: written `*kpAvatarImage`, or as an attribute, `kpAvatarImage`. The picture, in either of two forms. `<img *kpAvatarImage="address" alt="…">` is in the page once the picture has loaded. `<img kpAvatarImage [src]="address" alt="…">` is the caller's own element, kept in the page as Base UI's `keepMounted` image: it loads the picture itself (`loading="lazy"` works), its own `src` is the address and is followed as it changes, and until it has loaded it is `aria-hidden`, with `data-loading` or `data-error` for the design to hide or fade it by. The root's `(loadingStatusChanged)` hears the loading either way. Write the structural form when the picture only has to appear once it is there; the attribute form when the element must be in the page from the start: to fade the picture in, to load it lazily, or to keep its attributes and place while it loads.
    - `*kpAvatarImage: string`: The directive's own value: `*kpAvatarImage="…"`. The picture's address, in the structural form: the element is in the page once it has loaded.
- `[kpAvatarFallback]` is `KpAvatarFallback`. Structural: written `*kpAvatarFallback`. `<span *kpAvatarFallback>`: what shows until the picture has loaded, or when it cannot. `{ delay: 600 }` waits that many milliseconds first, so a picture that loads sooner never lets it be seen.
    - `*kpAvatarFallback: { delay?: number | undefined } | ""`: The directive's own value: `*kpAvatarFallback="…"`. Its options: `{ delay: 600 }` waits that many milliseconds before showing. Read once. Default: no wait.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The frame the image and its stand-in share.
    - `data-image-loading-status="idle | loading | loaded | error"`: Where the picture is in its loading: `idle` while it has no address.
- image: The picture. In the page once it has loaded; with `keepMounted` (on Angular, the attribute form) in the page all along, `aria-hidden` until it has loaded.
    - `data-loading`: Present while the picture loads, on an image kept in the page.
    - `data-error`: Present when the picture cannot load, on an image kept in the page.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `fallback`.

### Button

```
import { KpButton } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Props:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `focusableWhenDisabled?: boolean`: Keeps a disabled button in the tab order, so what it would do can still be read.
- `nativeButton?: boolean`: `false` when the element is not a `<button>`: it is given a button's role, a place in the tab order and its keys (Enter, Space). A link that navigates (an `<a>` or `<area>` with an `href`) stays a link: no role is written over its own, it keeps its own place in the tab order and its own Enter, and Space does not press it; disabled, it is still blocked. Default `true`.

`[kpButton]` is `KpButton`. `exportAs: "kpButton"`. On a `<button>`, or with `[nativeButton]="false"` on another element that acts as one; on a link that navigates (`<a href>`), it stays a link.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Calendar

```
import { KpCalendar, KpCalendarHeading, KpCalendarPrevious, KpCalendarNext, KpCalendarMonths, KpCalendarGrid, KpCalendarWeekdays, KpCalendarHeadCell, KpCalendarWeeks, KpCalendarCell, KpCalendarDay, KpCalendarInput } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpCalendar]`, `[kpCalendarHeading]`, `[kpCalendarPrevious]`, `[kpCalendarNext]`, `[kpCalendarMonths]`, `[kpCalendarGrid]`, `[kpCalendarWeekdays]`, `[kpCalendarHeadCell]`, `[kpCalendarWeeks]`, `[kpCalendarCell]`, `[kpCalendarDay]`, `input[kpCalendarInput]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpCalendar
  *kpCalendarMonths (optional)
    kpCalendarHeading
    kpCalendarGrid
      *kpCalendarWeekdays
        kpCalendarHeadCell (repeated)
      *kpCalendarWeeks
        kpCalendarCell (repeated)
          kpCalendarDay
  kpCalendarPrevious
  kpCalendarNext
  input[kpCalendarInput]
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: CalendarValueOf<Mode>`: One day; with `mode="range"` a first and a last; with `mode="multiple"` a list: `[(value)]`. Typed by `mode`.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<CalendarValueOf<Mode>>`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `mode?: Mode`: One day (the default), a first and a last (`"range"`), or any number (`"multiple"`).
- `required?: boolean`: A chosen day stays chosen: pressed again it is kept, and with `mode="multiple"` the last day cannot be taken away. Without it, a second press on the chosen day empties the value.
- `minDays?: number`: With `mode="multiple"`: the fewest days that can be left chosen.
- `maxDays?: number`: With `mode="multiple"`: the most days that can be chosen.
- `months?: number`: How many months are shown side by side, each drawn by `*kpCalendarMonths`. Default `1`.
- `pagedNavigation?: boolean`: With several `months`: Previous and Next turn them all rather than one month.
- `[(month)]: string`: The first day of the month shown (any day of it): `[(month)]`.
- `defaultMonth?: string`: The month it starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once.
- `defaultFocusedValue?: string`: The day it opens on, focusable when Tab reaches the grid. It is also the month it opens on, unless `month` or `defaultMonth` says another: then the stop for Tab is a chosen day of the months shown, today, or their first day.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region its names, first day of the week and calendar follow. The week begins where the region begins it, or on the day a `-u-fw-` extension names (`"en-US-u-fw-mon"`). Default `"en-US"`.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its months are laid out in, when it is not the Gregorian one.
- `min?: string`: The first and the last day that can be chosen.
- `max?: string`: The last day that can be chosen.
- `isDateUnavailable?: (date: string) => boolean`: Days that cannot be chosen, though they can be reached: a day off, a day taken.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no day can be chosen.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is: the days can be moved through, and none can be chosen.
- `fixedWeeks?: boolean`: Always six rows, so the calendar is one height in every month.
- `name?: string`: The name its hidden input (`kpCalendarInput`) submits the value under.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: CalendarValueOf<Mode>; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as a day is about to be chosen: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.
- `(monthChanged): { month: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Another month is about to be shown: its first day, and `details.cancel()`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpCalendar]` is `KpCalendar`. `exportAs: "kpCalendar"`. Generic: `<Mode extends CalendarMode = CalendarMode>`. Its props are above.
- `[kpCalendarHeading]` is `KpCalendarHeading`. Names the month shown, unless the element has content of its own: then that is what it says, and the live region reads it as the month changes.
- `[kpCalendarPrevious]` is `KpCalendarPrevious`.
- `[kpCalendarNext]` is `KpCalendarNext`.
- `[kpCalendarMonths]` is `KpCalendarMonths`. Structural: written `*kpCalendarMonths`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `CalendarMonth`. `<div *kpCalendarMonths="let month">`: once for each month shown, side by side. The parts inside each are that month's. Left out for one month.
- `[kpCalendarGrid]` is `KpCalendarGrid`. The table of a month's days: a grid the arrows move in, from one month shown into the next.
- `[kpCalendarWeekdays]` is `KpCalendarWeekdays`. Structural: written `*kpCalendarWeekdays`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `CalendarWeekday`. `<th *kpCalendarWeekdays="let weekday">`: once for each day of the week.
- `[kpCalendarHeadCell]` is `KpCalendarHeadCell`. A column's heading: a day of the week.
    - `weekday: CalendarWeekday`: Required. The day of the week it heads: an entry `Calendar.Weekdays` gave.
- `[kpCalendarWeeks]` is `KpCalendarWeeks`. Structural: written `*kpCalendarWeeks`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `readonly CalendarDay[]`. `<tr *kpCalendarWeeks="let week">`: once for each week of the month shown.
- `[kpCalendarCell]` is `KpCalendarCell`.
    - `date: string`: Required. The day it holds, as `*kpCalendarWeeks` gave it; a `kpCalendarDay` inside takes it too.
- `[kpCalendarDay]` is `KpCalendarDay`.
    - `date?: string`: The day it is the button of. Left out, its `kpCalendarCell`'s.
- `input[kpCalendarInput]` is `KpCalendarInput`. `<input kpCalendarInput>`: the hidden input the value is submitted by, with a `name`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The calendar.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
- previous: Shows the month before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Shows the month after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- cell: A day's cell.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- day: The button for a day.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `heading`, `grid`, `headCell` and `input`.

### Carousel

```
import { KpCarousel, KpCarouselViewport, KpCarouselItem, KpCarouselPrevious, KpCarouselNext, KpCarouselIndicator } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpCarousel]`, `[kpCarouselViewport]`, `[kpCarouselItem]`, `[kpCarouselPrevious]`, `[kpCarouselNext]`, `[kpCarouselIndicator]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpCarousel
  kpCarouselViewport
    kpCarouselItem (repeated)
  kpCarouselPrevious
  kpCarouselNext
  kpCarouselIndicator (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(index)]: number`: Which slide is at the start of the view: `[(index)]`.
- `defaultIndex?: number`: The slide it starts at, when the caller does not hold `index`. Read once. Default `0`.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the slides go across (the default) or down.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether going on from the last slide comes round to the first.
- `(indexChanged): { index: number; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as another slide is about to be at the start of the view: `details.cancel()` keeps the index as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpCarousel]` is `KpCarousel`. `exportAs: "kpCarousel"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpCarouselViewport]` is `KpCarouselViewport`.
- `[kpCarouselItem]` is `KpCarouselItem`.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among the slides, from 0. Left out, its place in the page, once it is there: give it on a page a server draws, which cannot count them.
- `[kpCarouselPrevious]` is `KpCarouselPrevious`.
- `[kpCarouselNext]` is `KpCarouselNext`.
- `[kpCarouselIndicator]` is `KpCarouselIndicator`.
    - `index: number`: Required. The slide it goes to, from 0.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The carousel: a region, named by the caller.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
- viewport: What scrolls. The slides are its children; the design snaps them (`scroll-snap-type`) and says whether a step glides (`scroll-behavior`).
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
- item: One slide.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
    - `data-current`: Present on the slide the view is at, and on its button.
- previous: Goes back a slide.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes on a slide.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: A button for one slide.
    - `data-current`: Present on the slide the view is at, and on its button.

### Checkbox

```
import { KpCheckbox, KpCheckboxIndicator } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpCheckbox]`, `[kpCheckboxIndicator]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpCheckbox
  *kpCheckboxIndicator
```

Props of its root:

- `[(checked)]: boolean`: Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Read once.
- `indeterminate?: boolean`: Neither checked nor unchecked: a parent of boxes that disagree.
- `parent?: boolean`: In a `kpCheckboxGroup` with `allValues`: the box that stands for them all, written anywhere inside the group. It is checked when every one is, mixed when some are, and it is not submitted; its `aria-controls` names the boxes. A press from mixed checks them all, the next unchecks them all, and the next brings back the set they were left in (left all checked or none, a press goes between all and none); a disabled box keeps its state. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value?: string`: What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `kpId?: string`: The id of the box's hidden native checkbox, not of the box: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.
- `(checkedChanged): { checked: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: The change with why it happened; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpCheckbox]` is `KpCheckbox`. `exportAs: "kpCheckbox"`. On the box's element. It draws the hidden native input inside it, which a form and a label reach. Its props are above.
- `[kpCheckboxIndicator]` is `KpCheckboxIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpCheckboxIndicator`. `<span *kpCheckboxIndicator>`: in the page while the box is checked or indeterminate. Its template is given nothing: a dash while mixed and a tick while checked are both written in it and chosen in CSS by the element's `data-indeterminate` (`[data-indeterminate] .tick`, `:not([data-indeterminate]) > .dash`, each `display: none`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The box. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-parent`: Present on the checkbox that stands for every box of its group.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while the box is checked or indeterminate. `data-indeterminate` and `data-checked` say which mark to draw, a dash or a tick: in CSS (`[data-indeterminate]`), or from the part's state. Through its exit the box is already unchecked, and both are absent.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### CheckboxGroup

```
import { KpCheckboxGroup } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Props:

- `[(value)]: readonly string[]`: The values of the checked checkboxes, when the caller holds them.
- `defaultValue?: readonly string[]`: The values checked at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `allValues?: readonly string[]`: The value of every checkbox of the group, for a parent checkbox: it is checked when all of them are, mixed when some are, and a press on it goes from the set they were left in to all, then none, then back. Its order names the boxes' elements (`<id>-0` …).
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every checkbox of the group.
- `kpId?: string`: The group's own id, and what its boxes' elements are named from (`<id>-0`, `<id>-1` …, by their place in `allValues`), which a parent box's `aria-controls` names. Inside a `Field`, the group takes the field's id instead.
- `(valueChanged): { value: string[]; details: ChangeDetails }`: The change with why it happened; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.

`[kpCheckboxGroup]` is `KpCheckboxGroup`. `exportAs: "kpCheckboxGroup"`. Checkboxes that hold one list of values. Each `kpCheckbox` with a `value` inside it is checked while the list has its value; with `allValues`, a `kpCheckbox` marked `parent` stands for them all.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group: `role="group"`, with its `id`. Name it with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` naming a heading of your own; inside a `Field`, the field's label names it and its description describes it. A checkbox anywhere inside it with a `value` is checked while the group's value holds it; one marked `parent`, anywhere inside it too, stands for every value of `allValues`, and its `aria-controls` names their boxes.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Collapsible

```
import { KpCollapsible, KpCollapsibleTrigger, KpCollapsiblePanel } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpCollapsible]`, `[kpCollapsibleTrigger]`, `[kpCollapsiblePanel]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpCollapsible
  kpCollapsibleTrigger (repeated)
  *kpCollapsiblePanel
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: its trigger does not open or close it.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: The change with why it happened; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpCollapsible]` is `KpCollapsible`. `exportAs: "kpCollapsible"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpCollapsibleTrigger]` is `KpCollapsibleTrigger`.
- `[kpCollapsiblePanel]` is `KpCollapsiblePanel`. Structural: written `*kpCollapsiblePanel`. `<div *kpCollapsiblePanel>`: in the page while open; `{ keepMounted: true }` keeps it, hidden.
    - `*kpCollapsiblePanel: { keepMounted?: boolean } | ""`: The directive's own value: `*kpCollapsiblePanel="…"`. Its options: `{ keepMounted: true }` keeps the panel in the page, hidden, while it is closed.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the trigger and the panel.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of the panel's entrance, as on the panel.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through the panel's exit, as on the panel.
- trigger: The button that opens and closes the panel.
    - `data-panel-open`: Present when the panel is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: The content. In the page while open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `--collapsible-panel-height`: The panel's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--collapsible-panel-width`: The panel's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

### ColorPicker

```
import { KpColorPicker, KpColorPickerArea, KpColorPickerAreaThumb, KpColorPickerChannelSlider, KpColorPickerChannelSliderTrack, KpColorPickerChannelSliderThumb, KpColorPickerChannelInput, KpColorPickerSwatch, KpColorPickerSwatchTrigger, KpColorPickerEyeDropperTrigger, KpColorPickerValueText, KpColorPickerFormatTrigger } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpColorPicker]`, `[kpColorPickerArea]`, `[kpColorPickerAreaThumb]`, `[kpColorPickerChannelSlider]`, `[kpColorPickerChannelSliderTrack]`, `[kpColorPickerChannelSliderThumb]`, `[kpColorPickerChannelInput]`, `[kpColorPickerSwatch]`, `[kpColorPickerSwatchTrigger]`, `[kpColorPickerEyeDropperTrigger]`, `[kpColorPickerValueText]`, `[kpColorPickerFormatTrigger]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpColorPicker
  kpColorPickerArea
    kpColorPickerAreaThumb
  kpColorPickerChannelSlider (repeated)
    kpColorPickerChannelSliderTrack
      kpColorPickerChannelSliderThumb
    kpColorPickerChannelSliderThumb (as above)
  kpColorPickerChannelInput (repeated)
  kpColorPickerSwatch (repeated)
  kpColorPickerSwatchTrigger (repeated)
  kpColorPickerEyeDropperTrigger
  kpColorPickerValueText
  kpColorPickerFormatTrigger
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: string`: The colour as text in `format`. Any format is read.
- `defaultValue?: string`: Read once. Default `#000000`.
- `[(format)]: ColorFormat`: How the value is written, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultFormat?: ColorFormat`: Read once. Default `"hex"`.
- `alpha?: boolean`: Whether the opacity can be chosen: the value then always carries its alpha.
- `thumbAlignment?: "center" | "edge"`: `"edge"` keeps a thumb inside its area or track at the ends of its range.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable; its value is still submitted.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed by the form. A colour always has a value, so this only says so.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around the picker.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the picker belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string, thumb: ColorPickerThumb, color: Hsva) => string`: What assistive technology reads for a thumb, when the written one is not enough.
- `(valueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Each step of a drag, each key, each colour typed or chosen; `details.cancel()` keeps it.
- `(valueCommitted): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: When the pointer lets go, after each key, when a typed channel is left: the value to save.
- `(formatChanged): { format: ColorFormat; details: ChangeDetails }`: When the format trigger goes to the next format; `details.cancel()` keeps it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpColorPicker]` is `KpColorPicker`. `exportAs: "kpColorPicker"`. On the element that holds the picker's parts. `[(value)]` is the colour as text in its format, `[(format)]` the format. It draws the hidden input a form reads, as its last child. Its props are above.
- `[kpColorPickerArea]` is `KpColorPickerArea`.
- `[kpColorPickerAreaThumb]` is `KpColorPickerAreaThumb`.
- `[kpColorPickerChannelSlider]` is `KpColorPickerChannelSlider`. What a pointer presses and drags on to move a channel: its track and thumb are inside it.
    - `channel: ColorPickerSliderChannel`: Required. The channel it moves: the hue, or the alpha.
    - `orientation?: Orientation`: The way its track runs. Default `horizontal`.
- `[kpColorPickerChannelSliderTrack]` is `KpColorPickerChannelSliderTrack`.
- `[kpColorPickerChannelSliderThumb]` is `KpColorPickerChannelSliderThumb`.
- `[kpColorPickerChannelInput]` is `KpColorPickerChannelInput`. On an `<input>`: one channel typed in, or the whole colour in hex. Its text is the core's.
    - `channel: ColorPickerInputChannel`: Required. The channel it is typed in, or `hex` for the whole colour.
- `[kpColorPickerSwatch]` is `KpColorPickerSwatch`.
- `[kpColorPickerSwatchTrigger]` is `KpColorPickerSwatchTrigger`. `exportAs: "kpColorPickerSwatchTrigger"`. A preset: pressed, the colour is this one. `state()` is its state, for the template (`#preset="kpColorPickerSwatchTrigger"`, `preset.state().selected`).
    - `value: string`: Required. The preset's colour, in any format.
- `[kpColorPickerEyeDropperTrigger]` is `KpColorPickerEyeDropperTrigger`. Picks a colour from the screen, where the browser can; hidden where it cannot.
- `[kpColorPickerValueText]` is `KpColorPickerValueText`. Says the colour in its format, unless the element has content of its own.
- `[kpColorPickerFormatTrigger]` is `KpColorPickerFormatTrigger`. Goes to the next format; says the current one, unless the element has content of its own.

A picker that opens from a swatch is a `Popover` inside the picker's root, the swatch drawn as its trigger (a `<button>`, given the swatch's `--color`); the parts in the popup find the picker through the portal. The root's `--color` does not reach them, since the portal is drawn at the end of `<body>`: a part in the popup paints from its own variables, listed below.

```
<div kpColorPicker [defaultValue]="'#3b82f6'">
  <ng-container kpPopover>
    <button kpPopoverTrigger kpColorPickerSwatch aria-label="Colour"></button>
    <ng-template kpPopoverPortal><div kpPopoverPositioner><div kpPopoverPopup>
      <div kpColorPickerArea><div kpColorPickerAreaThumb></div></div>
      <div kpColorPickerChannelSlider [channel]="'hue'">
        <div kpColorPickerChannelSliderTrack><div kpColorPickerChannelSliderThumb></div></div>
      </div>
    </div></div></ng-template>
  </ng-container>
</div>
```

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the picker's parts. It holds the hidden input a form reads, and the colour for anything inside to paint with.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-format="hex | rgb | hsl"`: How the value is written.
    - `--color`: The colour, with its alpha.
- area: The two-dimensional field a pointer presses and drags on: saturation across, the way the text runs, and brightness up. A design paints it from its hue: `linear-gradient(to top, #000, transparent), linear-gradient(to right, #fff, var(--hue-color))` (`to left` for the second where the text runs right to left). It writes `touch-action: none` inline, so a finger drags the thumb, not the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `--hue-color`: The colour's hue at full saturation and brightness.
- areaThumb: What is dragged in the area, and what the arrows move: a slider in two dimensions to assistive technology, its text saying both. Its place is written on it inline, and a design does not set these: `position: absolute`, `inset-inline-start` and `bottom` at its saturation and brightness, and a `translate` that centres it on that point (with `thumbAlignment: "edge"`, one that keeps it inside the area). The area is what it is placed in, so the area needs `position: relative`.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `--saturation`: Its place across, as a share of the area: the saturation.
    - `--brightness`: Its place up, as a share of the area: the brightness.
    - `--color`: The colour under it, without its alpha.
- channelSlider: What a pointer presses and drags on to move the hue or the alpha. It holds the track and the thumb. It takes `channel` and `orientation`. It writes `touch-action: none` inline, so a finger drags the thumb, not the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `data-channel="hue | alpha"`: The channel the slider moves.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
- channelSliderTrack: The channel's whole range: what a design paints the hues or the alpha on. Both run from the inline start (the bottom of a vertical track): the hue from 0 to 360, `linear-gradient(to right, #f00, #ff0, #0f0, #0ff, #00f, #f0f, #f00)`, and the alpha from none to whole, `linear-gradient(to right, transparent, var(--color))` over a checkerboard of the design's own (`to left` where the text runs right to left, `to top` on a vertical track).
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `data-channel="hue | alpha"`: The channel the slider moves.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `--color`: The colour without its alpha: the end of an alpha track.
    - `--hue-color`: The colour's hue at full saturation and brightness.
- channelSliderThumb: What is dragged, and what the keyboard moves: a slider to assistive technology, its range 0 to 360 for the hue and 0 to 100 for the alpha. Its place on the track is written on it inline, and a design does not set these: `position: absolute`, `inset-inline-start` at its share of the range and `top: 50%` (on a vertical track, `bottom` and `left: 50%`), and a `translate` that centres it there (with `thumbAlignment: "edge"`, one that keeps it inside the track). The element it is in (the track, or the slider) needs `position: relative`.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `data-channel="hue | alpha"`: The channel the slider moves.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `--color`: The colour under it: the pure hue, or the colour at its alpha.
- channelInput: A text input for one channel (`hex`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `hue`, `saturation`, `lightness`, `alpha`). What is typed is taken when it is a colour or a number in range, and put back when focus leaves while it is not.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-channel="hex | red | green | blue | hue | saturation | lightness | alpha"`: The channel the input is typed in.
- swatch: Shows the current colour.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `--color`: The colour, with its alpha.
- swatchTrigger: A preset colour, given as `value`: pressed, the colour is this one.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-selected`: Present while the colour is this one.
    - `--color`: The preset's colour, with its alpha.
- eyeDropperTrigger: Picks a colour from the screen with the browser's eye dropper. Hidden where the browser has none, and on a server.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
- valueText: The colour, written in its format.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-format="hex | rgb | hsl"`: How the value is written.
- formatTrigger: Goes to the next format: hex, then rgb, then hsl.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-format="hex | rgb | hsl"`: How the value is written.

### Combobox

```
import { KpCombobox, KpComboboxInput, KpComboboxTrigger, KpComboboxValue, KpComboboxClear, KpComboboxChips, KpComboboxChip, KpComboboxChipRemove, KpComboboxPortal, KpComboboxBackdrop, KpComboboxPositioner, KpComboboxPopup, KpComboboxList, KpComboboxCollection, KpComboboxGroup, KpComboboxGroupLabel, KpComboboxSeparator, KpComboboxItem, KpComboboxItemIndicator, KpComboboxEmpty, KpComboboxStatus, KpComboboxHiddenInput } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpCombobox]`, `input[kpComboboxInput]`, `[kpComboboxTrigger]`, `[kpComboboxValue]`, `[kpComboboxClear]`, `[kpComboboxChips]`, `[kpComboboxChip]`, `[kpComboboxChipRemove]`, `[kpComboboxPortal]`, `[kpComboboxBackdrop]`, `[kpComboboxPositioner]`, `[kpComboboxPopup]`, `[kpComboboxList]`, `[kpComboboxCollection]`, `[kpComboboxGroup]`, `[kpComboboxGroupLabel]`, `[kpComboboxSeparator]`, `[kpComboboxItem]`, `[kpComboboxItemIndicator]`, `[kpComboboxEmpty]`, `[kpComboboxStatus]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpCombobox
  input[kpComboboxInput]
  kpComboboxTrigger
    *kpComboboxValue (optional, or kpComboboxValue as an attribute)
  *kpComboboxPortal
    kpComboboxBackdrop (optional)
    kpComboboxPositioner
      kpComboboxPopup
        input[kpComboboxInput] (as above)
        kpComboboxList (optional)
          *kpComboboxCollection (optional)
            kpComboboxItem (repeated, as above)
            kpComboboxGroup (optional, repeated, as above)
          kpComboboxGroup (optional, repeated)
            *kpComboboxCollection (optional, as above)
            kpComboboxItem (repeated)
              *kpComboboxItemIndicator
            kpComboboxGroupLabel
          kpComboboxSeparator (repeated)
        *kpComboboxCollection (optional, as above)
        *kpComboboxEmpty
        kpComboboxStatus (optional)
  kpComboboxPopup (as above)
  kpComboboxStatus (optional, as above)
  *kpComboboxClear
  kpComboboxChips
    input[kpComboboxInput] (as above)
    kpComboboxChip (repeated)
      kpComboboxChipRemove
  input[kpComboboxHiddenInput] (Angular only)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: (Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null)`: With `[multiple]="true"`, the chosen values.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null>`: The value it starts with (with `multiple`, the values), when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `[(inputValue)]: string`: What the input says, `[(inputValue)]`. With `kpAutocomplete` the text is `[(value)]`.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once.
- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Its value can be read and not changed: the list still opens and can be gone through, but no press and no Enter chooses, nothing typed is taken, and its clear and chip buttons do nothing. Its value is still submitted.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[] | readonly ComboboxGroupData<Value>[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The values with their labels: a list of them, groups of them (`{ value, items }`), or the labels by value. With a `*kpComboboxCollection` it is the list itself: the combobox filters it, and the collection draws what is left.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed; `null` shows every item.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `multiple?: Multiple`: Several values, each shown as a chip: `value` and `valueChanged` then hold a list. Bound to `true` (`[multiple]="true"`), it types them so. The bare attribute, or a bound boolean, works the same, and then `value` takes either and `valueChanged` is typed as one value: Angular's compiler gives a type parameter it cannot infer `any`, so only a literal `true` says it.
- `inline?: boolean`: The list is always in the page, with no popup: a command palette.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page: each item is then given its `index`.
- `presentation?: Presentation`: How the list opens: `"sheet"` from the bottom edge, modal, with a backdrop, the input then in the popup; `"auto"` a sheet on a narrow touch screen. Default `"popup"`.
- `sheetBelow?: number`: With `presentation="auto"`: the viewport's width under which a coarse pointer opens a sheet. Default 640.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: The first item shown for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter chooses it. Off by default.
- `itemToStringLabel?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the input shows for one, and what is filtered.
- `itemToStringValue?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the form is sent for one.
- `mode?: "list" | "both" | "inline" | "none"`: With `kpAutocomplete`: `"none"` shows the suggestions as the caller draws them; `"both"` and `"inline"` write the rest of the first that begins with what is typed into the input.
- `openOnInputClick?: boolean`: With `kpAutocomplete`: a press on the input opens the list.
- `(valueChanged): { value: true extends Multiple ? (false extends Multiple ? Value | null : Value[]) : Value | null details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as a value is about to be chosen or cleared (with `multiple`, added or taken away, with the values there would then be): `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(inputValueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the input's text is about to change; `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpCombobox]` is `KpCombobox`. `exportAs: "kpCombobox"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown, Multiple extends boolean = false>`. `kpAutocomplete` is a combobox whose text is the value: `[(value)]` is the text, and the list only suggests. Its parts are the combobox's directives. Its props are above.
- `input[kpComboboxInput]` is `KpComboboxInput`. `<input kpComboboxInput>`: what is typed filters the list, which is placed against it.
- `[kpComboboxTrigger]` is `KpComboboxTrigger`.
- `[kpComboboxValue]` is `KpComboboxValue`. Structural or not: written `*kpComboboxValue`, or as an attribute, `kpComboboxValue`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `ComboboxShown`. `<span kpComboboxValue [placeholder]="'Pick one'">` says the chosen value's label, or its placeholder while nothing is chosen; with `multiple`, the chosen labels with commas between. An element with content of its own says that instead. `<ng-container *kpComboboxValue="let shown">` draws its own content instead, with what is chosen: `shown.value` and `shown.label`, with `multiple` `shown.values` and `shown.labels`, in the order they were chosen. For a button that is the combobox, its input inside the popup.
    - `placeholder?: string`: Shown while nothing is chosen.
- `[kpComboboxClear]` is `KpComboboxClear`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxClear`. `<button *kpComboboxClear>`: empties the input and the value; in the page while there is something to clear.
- `[kpComboboxChips]` is `KpComboboxChips`. With `multiple`: what holds the chips and the input.
- `[kpComboboxChip]` is `KpComboboxChip`. With `multiple`: one chosen value. Its `value` is what its remove button takes away.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. The chosen value this chip stands for.
- `[kpComboboxChipRemove]` is `KpComboboxChipRemove`.
- `[kpComboboxPortal]` is `KpComboboxPortal`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpComboboxBackdrop]` is `KpComboboxBackdrop`. `<div kpComboboxBackdrop>`, in the portal: what lies over the page behind the list.
- `[kpComboboxPositioner]` is `KpComboboxPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpComboboxPopup]` is `KpComboboxPopup`.
- `[kpComboboxList]` is `KpComboboxList`. The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
- `[kpComboboxCollection]` is `KpComboboxCollection`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxCollection`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `ComboboxEntry`. `<ng-container *kpComboboxCollection="let entry">` draws the list from the root's `items`: once for each item left for what was typed, or for each group that has items left. With `of` (`*kpComboboxCollection="let item; of: group"`), for each of that group's items left. The root then filters, and no item hides itself.
    - `of?: ComboboxEntry`: Written after the directive's value: `*kpComboboxCollection="…; of: …"`. A group the root's `items` gave: its items left are then what is drawn.
- `[kpComboboxGroup]` is `KpComboboxGroup`. Items that belong together, named by their `kpComboboxGroupLabel`. Hidden while none is shown.
- `[kpComboboxGroupLabel]` is `KpComboboxGroupLabel`. Names the group it is in. With no group around it, it is plain text.
- `[kpComboboxSeparator]` is `KpComboboxSeparator`. A line between groups.
- `[kpComboboxItem]` is `KpComboboxItem`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the combobox's value is while this item is chosen.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered and what the input shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
- `[kpComboboxItemIndicator]` is `KpComboboxItemIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxItemIndicator`. `<span *kpComboboxItemIndicator>`: in the page while its item is the chosen one.
- `[kpComboboxEmpty]` is `KpComboboxEmpty`. Structural: written `*kpComboboxEmpty`. `<div *kpComboboxEmpty>`: in the page while no item is shown for what was typed.
- `[kpComboboxStatus]` is `KpComboboxStatus`. Says how the list stands ("3 results", "Loading") to software that reads the page, as its text changes. Keep it in the page and change what it holds: inside the popup, or beside the input.
- `input[kpComboboxHiddenInput]` is `KpComboboxHiddenInput`. `<input kpComboboxHiddenInput>`: submits the value with the form around it. Angular only.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list, which is placed against it, or against the chips' box when it is in one. Inside the popup, it takes focus while the popup is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the list: a press on it closes the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry. As a sheet it is not placed, and carries none.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list. As a sheet, a design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: As a sheet, once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value. It is in the page while there is something to clear (the text, for an autocomplete; else what is chosen), and through its exit; `keepMounted` keeps it there.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is something to clear.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- chip: One chosen value. The arrows reach it from the start of the input, and Backspace or Delete on it takes it away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- chipRemove: A chip's button that takes its value away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `groupLabel`, `separator`, `itemIndicator`, `empty`, `status` and `chips`.

### Command

```
import { KpCommand, KpCommandInput, KpCommandList, KpCommandEmpty, KpCommandGroup, KpCommandGroupHeading, KpCommandItem, KpCommandSeparator } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpCommand]`, `[kpCommandInput]`, `[kpCommandList]`, `[kpCommandEmpty]`, `[kpCommandGroup]`, `[kpCommandGroupHeading]`, `[kpCommandItem]`, `[kpCommandSeparator]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpCommand
  kpCommandInput
  kpCommandList
    *kpCommandEmpty
    kpCommandGroup (optional, repeated)
      kpCommandGroupHeading
      kpCommandItem (repeated)
    kpCommandSeparator (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(inputValue)]: string`: What the input says.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string, keywords: readonly string[]) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed; `null` shows every item.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether a step past an end of the list goes round to the other.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: Whether the first item shown is highlighted from the start. Default: `true`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed or chosen.
- `(inputValueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the input's text is about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(itemSelected): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: An item was chosen.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpCommand]` is `KpCommand`. `exportAs: "kpCommand"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpCommandInput]` is `KpCommandInput`.
- `[kpCommandList]` is `KpCommandList`.
- `[kpCommandEmpty]` is `KpCommandEmpty`. Structural: written `*kpCommandEmpty`. `<div *kpCommandEmpty>`: in the page while no item is shown for what was typed.
- `[kpCommandGroup]` is `KpCommandGroup`. Items under a `kpCommandGroupHeading`. Hidden while none of them is shown.
- `[kpCommandGroupHeading]` is `KpCommandGroupHeading`. A group's name.
- `[kpCommandItem]` is `KpCommandItem`.
    - `value?: string`: What `itemSelected` is told; its `label`, or its text, when left out.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered; the item's text when left out.
    - `keywords?: readonly string[]`: Other words the item answers to.
- `[kpCommandSeparator]` is `KpCommandSeparator`. A line between groups: gone while something is typed, unless `alwaysRender`.
    - `alwaysRender?: boolean`: Stays while something is typed.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A list of commands with the input that filters it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list; focus stays in it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- list: The commands.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One command.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `empty`, `group`, `groupHeading` and `separator`.

### ContextMenu

```
import { KpMenu, KpContextMenuTrigger, KpMenuPortal, KpMenuPositioner, KpMenuPopup, KpMenuArrow, KpMenuItem, KpMenuLinkItem, KpMenuGroup, KpMenuGroupLabel, KpMenuSeparator, KpMenuCheckboxItem, KpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator, KpMenuRadioGroup, KpMenuRadioItem, KpMenuRadioItemIndicator, KpMenuSubmenuRoot, KpMenuSubmenuTrigger } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpContextMenu]`, `[kpContextMenuTrigger]`, `[kpMenuPortal]`, `[kpMenuPositioner]`, `[kpMenuPopup]`, `[kpMenuArrow]`, `[kpMenuItem]`, `a[kpMenuLinkItem]`, `[kpMenuGroup]`, `[kpMenuGroupLabel]`, `[kpMenuSeparator]`, `[kpMenuCheckboxItem]`, `[kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator]`, `[kpMenuRadioGroup]`, `[kpMenuRadioItem]`, `[kpMenuRadioItemIndicator]`, `[kpMenuSubmenuRoot]`, `[kpMenuSubmenuTrigger]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpContextMenu
  kpContextMenuTrigger
  *kpMenuPortal
    kpMenuPositioner
      kpMenuPopup
        kpMenuArrow
        kpMenuGroup (optional, repeated)
          kpMenuItem (repeated)
          a[kpMenuLinkItem] (repeated)
          kpMenuGroupLabel
          kpMenuCheckboxItem (repeated)
            *kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator
          kpMenuRadioGroup (repeated)
            kpMenuRadioItem (repeated)
              *kpMenuRadioItemIndicator
          kpMenuSubmenuRoot (repeated)
            *kpMenuPortal (as above)
            kpMenuSubmenuTrigger
        kpMenuSeparator (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open. Not for a submenu.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpContextMenu]` is `KpMenu`. `exportAs: "kpMenu"`. `kpContextMenu` in place of `kpMenu` is a menu for an area of the page, opened at the pointer: its trigger is `kpContextMenuTrigger`, its other parts the menu's. Its props are above.
- `[kpContextMenuTrigger]` is `KpContextMenuTrigger`. The area a secondary press, or a long press on a touch screen, opens a `kpContextMenu` in.
- `[kpMenuPortal]` is `KpMenuPortal`. Structural: written `*kpMenuPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpMenuPositioner]` is `KpMenuPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpMenuPopup]` is `KpMenuPopup`.
- `[kpMenuArrow]` is `KpMenuArrow`.
- `[kpMenuItem]` is `KpMenuItem`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does.
- `a[kpMenuLinkItem]` is `KpMenuLinkItem`. `<a kpMenuLinkItem href="…">`: an item that is a link.
