    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does.
- `[kpMenuGroup]` is `KpMenuGroup`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `[kpMenuGroupLabel]` is `KpMenuGroupLabel`. Names the group it is in. With no group around it, it is plain text.
- `[kpMenuSeparator]` is `KpMenuSeparator`. A line between items.
- `[kpMenuCheckboxItem]` is `KpMenuCheckboxItem`. `exportAs: "kpMenuCheckboxItem"`.
    - `[(checked)]: boolean`: Whether the item is checked, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Whether the item starts checked, when the caller does not hold `checked`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does not.
    - `(checkedChanged): { checked: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the item is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `[kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator]` is `KpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator`. `<span *kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator>`: in the page while its item is checked.
- `[kpMenuRadioGroup]` is `KpMenuRadioGroup`. `exportAs: "kpMenuRadioGroup"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`.
    - `[(value)]: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
    - `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Value> | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
    - `(valueChanged): { value: Value; details: ChangeDetails }`: Told an item's own value, never `null`: a press chooses, and nothing takes the choice back.
- `[kpMenuRadioItem]` is `KpMenuRadioItem`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the radio group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does not.
- `[kpMenuRadioItemIndicator]` is `KpMenuRadioItemIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpMenuRadioItemIndicator`. `<span *kpMenuRadioItemIndicator>`: in the page while its item is the chosen one.
- `[kpMenuSubmenuRoot]` is `KpMenuSubmenuRoot`. `exportAs: "kpMenuSubmenuRoot"`. A menu that one of this menu's items opens. Its trigger is `kpMenuSubmenuTrigger`.
    - `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
    - `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
    - `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open. Not for a submenu.
    - `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `[kpMenuSubmenuTrigger]` is `KpMenuSubmenuTrigger`. On the item of a menu that opens the submenu around it (`kpMenuSubmenuRoot`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The area a secondary press, or a long press on a touch screen, opens the menu in.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss | group"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed its trigger or an item, `dismiss` when Escape closed it, `group` when focus or the pointer went from one menu of a bar to another.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `groupLabel` and `separator`.

### DateField

```
import { KpDateField, KpDateFieldSegments, KpDateFieldSegment, KpDateFieldInput } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpDateField]`, `[kpDateFieldSegments]`, `[kpDateFieldSegment]`, `input[kpDateFieldInput]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpDateField
  *kpDateFieldSegments
    kpDateFieldSegment (repeated)
  input[kpDateFieldInput]
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: string | null`: The day typed, once all of it is: `[(value)]`.
- `defaultValue?: string | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region that order the day, the month and the year. Default `"en-US"`.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its parts are typed in, when it is not the Gregorian one: an instance from `@internationalized/date`. The value is still an ISO day.
- `min?: string`: The first and the last day it takes: outside them it says it is invalid.
- `max?: string`: The last day it takes.
- `placeholders?: Partial<Record<DateUnit, string>>`: What an empty part shows. Default: `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy`, `era`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: a date left half typed is then invalid (`data-invalid`).
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under, by its hidden input.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: string | null; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the day is about to change, once all of it is typed or as it is cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpDateField]` is `KpDateField`. `exportAs: "kpDateField"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpDateFieldSegments]` is `KpDateFieldSegments`. Structural: written `*kpDateFieldSegments`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `DateFieldSegment`. `<span *kpDateFieldSegments="let segment">`: once for each piece of the date.
- `[kpDateFieldSegment]` is `KpDateFieldSegment`. One piece: a part that is typed, or what stands between two. It writes its own text.
    - `segment: DateFieldSegment`: Required. The piece it is: an entry `DateField.Segments` gave.
- `input[kpDateFieldInput]` is `KpDateFieldInput`. `<input kpDateFieldInput>`: the hidden input it is submitted by.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The field: a group of the date's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="era | day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is: the era only in a calendar of several eras.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `input`.

### DatePicker

```
import { KpDatePicker, KpDatePickerField, KpDateFieldSegments, KpDateFieldSegment, KpDateFieldInput, KpPopoverTrigger, KpPopoverPortal, KpPopoverPositioner, KpPopoverPopup, KpDatePickerCalendar, KpCalendarHeading, KpCalendarPrevious, KpCalendarNext, KpCalendarMonths, KpCalendarGrid, KpCalendarWeekdays, KpCalendarHeadCell, KpCalendarWeeks, KpCalendarCell, KpCalendarDay, KpDatePickerClear, KpDatePickerPreset } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpDatePicker]`, `[kpDatePickerField]`, `[kpDateFieldSegments]`, `[kpDateFieldSegment]`, `input[kpDateFieldInput]`, `[kpPopoverTrigger]`, `[kpPopoverPortal]`, `[kpPopoverPositioner]`, `[kpPopoverPopup]`, `[kpDatePickerCalendar]`, `[kpCalendarHeading]`, `[kpCalendarPrevious]`, `[kpCalendarNext]`, `[kpCalendarMonths]`, `[kpCalendarGrid]`, `[kpCalendarWeekdays]`, `[kpCalendarHeadCell]`, `[kpCalendarWeeks]`, `[kpCalendarCell]`, `[kpCalendarDay]`, `[kpDatePickerClear]`, `[kpDatePickerPreset]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpDatePicker
  kpDatePickerField (repeated)
    *kpDateFieldSegments
      kpDateFieldSegment (repeated)
    input[kpDateFieldInput]
  kpPopoverTrigger
  *kpPopoverPortal
    kpPopoverPositioner
      kpPopoverPopup
        kpDatePickerCalendar
          *kpCalendarMonths (optional)
            kpCalendarHeading
            kpCalendarGrid
              *kpCalendarWeekdays
                kpCalendarHeadCell (repeated)
              *kpCalendarWeeks
                kpCalendarCell (repeated)
                  kpCalendarDay
          kpCalendarPrevious
          kpCalendarNext
  kpDatePickerClear (optional)
  kpDatePickerPreset (optional, repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: DatePickerValueOf<Mode>`: The day; with `mode="range"` a first and a last: `[(value)]`. Typed by `mode`.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<DatePickerValueOf<Mode>>`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `mode?: Mode`: One day (the default), or a first and a last (`"range"`): two `kpDatePickerField`s, `range="start"` and `range="end"`. Read once.
- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether the calendar is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the calendar starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region of the field and the calendar. Give it: a server does not know.
- `min?: string`: The first and the last day that can be typed or picked.
- `max?: string`: The last day that can be typed or picked.
- `isDateUnavailable?: CalendarProps["isDateUnavailable"]`: Days that cannot be picked in the calendar.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarProps["calendarSystem"]`: The calendar its months are laid out in and its field typed in, when it is not the Gregorian one. The value is an ISO day whatever it is.
- `fixedWeeks?: boolean`: Always six rows of days.
- `months?: number`: How many months the calendar shows side by side.
- `pagedNavigation?: boolean`: With several `months`: Previous and Next turn them all rather than one month.
- `[(month)]: string`: The first day of the month the calendar shows (any day of it): `[(month)]`.
- `defaultMonth?: string`: The month the calendar starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once.
- `placeholders?: DateFieldProps["placeholders"]`: What an empty part of the field shows.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid, and the day picked, pressed again in the calendar, stays picked. Without it, that press empties the field and closes the calendar.
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: DatePickerValueOf<Mode>; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the value is about to change, typed, picked, pressed or cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was. A range is heard as each end comes, its other end `null` until it is there too.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the calendar is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(monthChanged): { month: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: The calendar is about to show another month: its first day, and `details.cancel()`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpDatePicker]` is `KpDatePicker`. `exportAs: "kpDatePicker"`. Generic: `<Mode extends DatePickerMode = DatePickerMode>`. A date field, and a calendar in a popover, with one value between them. On any element, or on `<ng-container>` to draw none. Inside it the date field's, the popover's and the calendar's own directives are its parts (`kpDateFieldSegments`, `kpPopoverTrigger`, `kpCalendarGrid` …), with `kpDatePickerField` and `kpDatePickerCalendar` for the two elements that hold them, and `kpDatePickerClear` and `kpDatePickerPreset` buttons. `[(value)]` is the day (with `mode="range"` the range), `[(open)]` whether the calendar shows, `[(month)]` the first day of the month it shows. Its props are above.
- `[kpDatePickerField]` is `KpDatePickerField`. The typed date: what holds its segments and its hidden input. With `mode="range"` there are two, `range="start"` and `range="end"`, each giving the date field's directives inside it their field.
    - `range?: "start" | "end"`: With `mode="range"`: which day of the range it is typed in, the first (`"start"`, the default) or the last (`"end"`).
- `[kpDateFieldSegments]` is `KpDateFieldSegments`. Structural: written `*kpDateFieldSegments`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `DateFieldSegment`. `<span *kpDateFieldSegments="let segment">`: once for each piece of the date.
- `[kpDateFieldSegment]` is `KpDateFieldSegment`. One piece: a part that is typed, or what stands between two. It writes its own text.
    - `segment: DateFieldSegment`: Required. The piece it is: an entry `DateField.Segments` gave.
- `input[kpDateFieldInput]` is `KpDateFieldInput`. `<input kpDateFieldInput>`: the hidden input it is submitted by.
- `[kpPopoverTrigger]` is `KpPopoverTrigger`.
    - `openOnHover?: boolean`: Whether the pointer resting on the trigger opens the popover too. A press and the keyboard still open it, and a press on one the pointer opened keeps it open. Default `false`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popover opens, in milliseconds. Default 300.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves a popover it opened closes, in milliseconds. Default 0.
- `[kpPopoverPortal]` is `KpPopoverPortal`. Structural: written `*kpPopoverPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpPopoverPositioner]` is `KpPopoverPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpPopoverPopup]` is `KpPopoverPopup`.
- `[kpDatePickerCalendar]` is `KpDatePickerCalendar`. The calendar: what holds its heading, its buttons and its grid.
- `[kpCalendarHeading]` is `KpCalendarHeading`. Names the month shown, unless the element has content of its own: then that is what it says, and the live region reads it as the month changes.
- `[kpCalendarPrevious]` is `KpCalendarPrevious`.
- `[kpCalendarNext]` is `KpCalendarNext`.
- `[kpCalendarMonths]` is `KpCalendarMonths`. Structural: written `*kpCalendarMonths`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `CalendarMonth`. `<div *kpCalendarMonths="let month">`: once for each month shown, side by side. The parts inside each are that month's. Left out for one month.
- `[kpCalendarGrid]` is `KpCalendarGrid`. The table of a month's days: a grid the arrows move in, from one month shown into the next.
- `[kpCalendarWeekdays]` is `KpCalendarWeekdays`. Structural: written `*kpCalendarWeekdays`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `CalendarWeekday`. `<th *kpCalendarWeekdays="let weekday">`: once for each day of the week.
- `[kpCalendarHeadCell]` is `KpCalendarHeadCell`. A column's heading: a day of the week.
    - `weekday: CalendarWeekday`: Required. The day of the week it heads: an entry `Calendar.Weekdays` gave.
- `[kpCalendarWeeks]` is `KpCalendarWeeks`. Structural: written `*kpCalendarWeeks`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `readonly CalendarDay[]`. `<tr *kpCalendarWeeks="let week">`: once for each week of the month shown.
- `[kpCalendarCell]` is `KpCalendarCell`.
    - `date: string`: Required. The day it holds, as `*kpCalendarWeeks` gave it; a `kpCalendarDay` inside takes it too.
- `[kpCalendarDay]` is `KpCalendarDay`.
    - `date?: string`: The day it is the button of. Left out, its `kpCalendarCell`'s.
- `[kpDatePickerClear]` is `KpDatePickerClear`. Empties the value, and gives focus to the field. Disabled while there is none.
- `[kpDatePickerPreset]` is `KpDatePickerPreset`. `<button kpDatePickerPreset [value]="…">`: makes the value the one it is given, pressed while it is.
    - `value: string | DatePickerRange`: Required. The value its press gives: a day, or with `mode="range"` a range.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- field: The field a day is typed in: with `mode: "range"`, one for the first day (`range="start"`) and one for the last (`range="end"`).
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="era | day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is: the era only in a calendar of several eras.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while the popover a press on this trigger opened is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed the trigger, `dismiss` when Escape closed it.
    - `--popup-width`: Its width: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old width and then the new one, for a transition between them.
    - `--popup-height`: Its height: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old height and then the new one, for a transition between them.
- calendar: The calendar.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
- previous: Shows the month before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Shows the month after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- cell: A day's cell.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- day: The button for a day.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- clear: Empties the value, and gives focus to the field. Disabled while there is none.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- preset: Makes the value the day, or the range, it is given. Pressed while the value is that.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while the value is the one it gives.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `input`, `heading`, `grid` and `headCell`.

### Dialog

```
import { KpDialog, KpDialogTrigger, KpDialogPortal, KpDialogBackdrop, KpDialogViewport, KpDialogPopup, KpDialogTitle, KpDialogDescription, KpDialogClose } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpDialog]`, `[kpDialogTrigger]`, `[kpDialogPortal]`, `[kpDialogBackdrop]`, `[kpDialogViewport]`, `[kpDialogPopup]`, `[kpDialogTitle]`, `[kpDialogDescription]`, `[kpDialogClose]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpDialog
  kpDialogTrigger
  *kpDialogPortal
    kpDialogBackdrop
    kpDialogViewport (optional)
      kpDialogPopup
        kpDialogTitle
        kpDialogDescription
        kpDialogClose
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal?: boolean`: Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `disablePointerDismissal?: boolean`: Keeps it open when the pointer presses outside it. Default `false`. Escape always closes it: a caller who must keep it open cancels the change whose `details.reason` is `"escape-key"`.
- `swipeDirection?: DrawerSide`: With `kpDrawer`: the way it is dragged to close it. Default: `"down"`.
- `snapPoints?: readonly DrawerSnapPoint[]`: With `kpDrawer`: places it rests at, each the share of itself that shows.
- `[(snapPoint)]: DrawerSnapPoint`: With `kpDrawer`: which of them it rests at, `[(snapPoint)]`.
- `defaultSnapPoint?: DrawerSnapPoint`: With `kpDrawer`: where it opens. Default: the smallest.
- `(snapPointChanged): { snapPoint: DrawerSnapPoint; details: ChangeDetails }`: With `kpDrawer`: heard as it is about to rest at another snap point; `details.cancel()` keeps it where it was.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpDialog]` is `KpDialog`. `exportAs: "kpDialog"`. On any element, or on `<ng-container>` to draw none. `kpDrawer` in place of `kpDialog` is a dialog that comes from an edge and is dragged back to it (`swipeDirection`): its parts are a dialog's (`kpDialogPopup` …). An alert dialog has a root of its own, `kpAlertDialog`. Its props are above.
- `[kpDialogTrigger]` is `KpDialogTrigger`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).
- `[kpDialogPortal]` is `KpDialogPortal`. Structural: written `*kpDialogPortal`. `<ng-template kpDialogPortal>` or `*kpDialogPortal`: its content at the end of the page while open.
- `[kpDialogBackdrop]` is `KpDialogBackdrop`.
- `[kpDialogViewport]` is `KpDialogViewport`. What a long dialog scrolls in, around its popup: it may be left out. A dialog's and an alert dialog's; a drawer lies at an edge of the page and has none.
- `[kpDialogPopup]` is `KpDialogPopup`.
- `[kpDialogTitle]` is `KpDialogTitle`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `[kpDialogDescription]` is `KpDialogDescription`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `[kpDialogClose]` is `KpDialogClose`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
- close: A button that closes the dialog.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `title` and `description`.

### Drawer

```
import { KpDialog, KpDialogTrigger, KpDialogPortal, KpDialogBackdrop, KpDialogPopup, KpDialogTitle, KpDialogDescription, KpDialogClose } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpDrawer]`, `[kpDialogTrigger]`, `[kpDialogPortal]`, `[kpDialogBackdrop]`, `[kpDialogPopup]`, `[kpDialogTitle]`, `[kpDialogDescription]`, `[kpDialogClose]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpDrawer
  kpDialogTrigger
  *kpDialogPortal
    kpDialogBackdrop
    kpDialogPopup
      kpDialogTitle
      kpDialogDescription
      kpDialogClose
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal?: boolean`: Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `disablePointerDismissal?: boolean`: Keeps it open when the pointer presses outside it. Default `false`. Escape always closes it: a caller who must keep it open cancels the change whose `details.reason` is `"escape-key"`.
- `swipeDirection?: DrawerSide`: With `kpDrawer`: the way it is dragged to close it. Default: `"down"`.
- `snapPoints?: readonly DrawerSnapPoint[]`: With `kpDrawer`: places it rests at, each the share of itself that shows.
- `[(snapPoint)]: DrawerSnapPoint`: With `kpDrawer`: which of them it rests at, `[(snapPoint)]`.
- `defaultSnapPoint?: DrawerSnapPoint`: With `kpDrawer`: where it opens. Default: the smallest.
- `(snapPointChanged): { snapPoint: DrawerSnapPoint; details: ChangeDetails }`: With `kpDrawer`: heard as it is about to rest at another snap point; `details.cancel()` keeps it where it was.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpDrawer]` is `KpDialog`. `exportAs: "kpDialog"`. On any element, or on `<ng-container>` to draw none. `kpDrawer` in place of `kpDialog` is a dialog that comes from an edge and is dragged back to it (`swipeDirection`): its parts are a dialog's (`kpDialogPopup` …). An alert dialog has a root of its own, `kpAlertDialog`. Its props are above.
- `[kpDialogTrigger]` is `KpDialogTrigger`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).
- `[kpDialogPortal]` is `KpDialogPortal`. Structural: written `*kpDialogPortal`. `<ng-template kpDialogPortal>` or `*kpDialogPortal`: its content at the end of the page while open.
- `[kpDialogBackdrop]` is `KpDialogBackdrop`.
- `[kpDialogPopup]` is `KpDialogPopup`.
- `[kpDialogTitle]` is `KpDialogTitle`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `[kpDialogDescription]` is `KpDialogDescription`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `[kpDialogClose]` is `KpDialogClose`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed the drawer.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: Always 1: the backdrop takes the design's own time to leave, however the drawer was thrown.
    - `--drawer-height`: While the drawer is dragged: the height of the drawer in front.
- popup: The drawer. A design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="up | down | left | right"`: The way it is dragged to close it.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while it rests whole, of several snap points.
    - `data-nested-drawer-open`: Present while another drawer is open over it.
    - `data-nested-drawer-swiping`: Present while a drawer over it is dragged.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
    - `--drawer-height`: Its height.
    - `--nested-drawers`: How many drawers are open over it.
    - `--drawer-frontmost-height`: The height of the drawer in front of every other, while this one is open.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: Once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest. A drawer thrown hard arrives sooner.
    - `--drawer-width`: Its width.
- close: A button that closes the dialog.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `title` and `description`.

### Editable

```
import { KpEditable, KpEditablePreview, KpEditableInput, KpEditableEditTrigger, KpEditableSubmitTrigger, KpEditableCancelTrigger } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpEditable]`, `[kpEditablePreview]`, `[kpEditableInput]`, `[kpEditableEditTrigger]`, `[kpEditableSubmitTrigger]`, `[kpEditableCancelTrigger]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpEditable
  kpEditablePreview
  kpEditableInput
  kpEditableEditTrigger (optional)
  kpEditableSubmitTrigger (optional)
  kpEditableCancelTrigger (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: string`: The text it holds: what the preview shows, and what editing starts from.
- `defaultValue?: string`: The text it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `[(editing)]: boolean`: Whether it is being edited, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultEditing?: boolean`: Read once.
- `placeholder?: string`: What the preview shows while the text is empty. Default `""`.
- `activation?: "focus" | "click" | "dblclick" | "none"`: What on the preview starts an edit. Default `"focus"`.
- `submitOnBlur?: boolean`: Whether focus leaving the input keeps the edit (the default) or drops it.
- `selectOnFocus?: boolean`: Whether the text is selected as editing starts. Default `true`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be edited.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, not editable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a field, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under; in a field, the field's by default.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the input belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: An edit about to be kept; `details.cancel()` keeps the text, and the edit open.
- `(editingChanged): { editing: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Editing about to start or end; `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpEditable]` is `KpEditable`. `exportAs: "kpEditable"`. On the element that holds the editable's parts. `[(value)]` is the text, `[(editing)]` whether it is being edited. With a name, its input is what a form reads. Its props are above.
- `[kpEditablePreview]` is `KpEditablePreview`. Says the text, or the placeholder while there is none, unless the element has content of its own.
- `[kpEditableInput]` is `KpEditableInput`. `<input kpEditableInput>` or `<textarea kpEditableInput>`: in the page always, hidden unless editing.
- `[kpEditableEditTrigger]` is `KpEditableEditTrigger`.
- `[kpEditableSubmitTrigger]` is `KpEditableSubmitTrigger`.
- `[kpEditableCancelTrigger]` is `KpEditableCancelTrigger`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A text edited in place. Enter keeps the edit (in a `<textarea>`, where Enter is a new line, Ctrl or ⌘ with Enter) and Escape drops it, focus going back to the edit trigger (or the preview where there is none); focus leaving the input keeps the edit, or drops it with `submitOnBlur` `false`. Inside a `Field` its input is the field's control: the field's label names it, and a press on the label starts an edit.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- preview: The text as it reads, or the placeholder while there is none: hidden while editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- input: Where the text is typed, an `<input>` or a `<textarea>`: hidden unless editing. It is named by the root's `id`, or in a `Field` by the field's; an `id` given to it is kept, so a `<label for>` names it.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- editTrigger: Starts an edit: hidden while editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- submitTrigger: Keeps what was typed: hidden unless editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- cancelTrigger: Drops what was typed: hidden unless editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.

### Field

```
import { KpField, KpFieldLabel, KpFieldControl, KpFieldDescription, KpFieldError, KpFieldValidity } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpField]`, `[kpFieldLabel]`, `[kpFieldControl]`, `[kpFieldDescription]`, `[kpFieldError]`, `[kpFieldValidity]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpField
  kpFieldLabel
  kpFieldControl
  kpFieldDescription
  *kpFieldError (repeated)
  *kpFieldValidity
```

Props of its root:

- `name?: string`: The control's name in the form.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables the field: its control cannot be changed, and its parts say so (`data-disabled`).
- `invalid?: boolean`: Invalid whatever the value: an error known from elsewhere.
- `validate?: ( value: string ) => string | readonly string[] | null | Promise<string | readonly string[] | null>`: The field's own check, after the browser's: a message or several when the value is wrong, `null` when it is right. It may answer later, with a promise.
- `validationMode?: ValidationMode`: When the value is checked; the form's by default, else `"onSubmit"`.
- `validationDebounceTime?: number`: With `"onChange"`, how long the value must rest before it is checked, in milliseconds. Default `0`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpField]` is `KpField`. `exportAs: "kpField"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpFieldLabel]` is `KpFieldLabel`.
- `[kpFieldControl]` is `KpFieldControl`. On the control: an `<input>`, a `<textarea>` or a `<select>`.
- `[kpFieldDescription]` is `KpFieldDescription`.
- `[kpFieldError]` is `KpFieldError`. Structural: written `*kpFieldError`. `<div *kpFieldError>`: in the page while something is wrong, with the message as its text unless it has content of its own. `*kpFieldError="'valueMissing'"` shows for only that finding of the browser's, `*kpFieldError="true"` always.
    - `*kpFieldError: ValidityKey | boolean | ""`: The directive's own value: `*kpFieldError="…"`. One of the browser's findings (`"valueMissing"`) to show for only that; `true` to show always.
- `[kpFieldValidity]` is `KpFieldValidity`. Structural: written `*kpFieldValidity`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `FieldValidity`. `<ng-container *kpFieldValidity="let validity">`: draws its template with the field's validity.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A control with its label, its description and its errors.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- label: The control's name: a press on it reaches the control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- control: The control: an input, a textarea or a select.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- description: More about the control, said after its name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- error: What is wrong with the value. In the page while it applies. Several, each with its own `match`, can be shown at once: each has an id of its own, and the control names them all.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

import { KpFieldset, KpFieldsetLegend } from "@kirana-ui/angular"

### FileUpload

```
import { KpFileUpload, KpFileUploadDropzone, KpFileUploadTrigger, KpFileUploadList, KpFileUploadItems, KpFileUploadItem, KpFileUploadItemName, KpFileUploadItemSize, KpFileUploadItemRemove, KpFileUploadClear } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpFileUpload]`, `[kpFileUploadDropzone]`, `[kpFileUploadTrigger]`, `[kpFileUploadList]`, `[kpFileUploadItems]`, `[kpFileUploadItem]`, `[kpFileUploadItemName]`, `[kpFileUploadItemSize]`, `[kpFileUploadItemRemove]`, `[kpFileUploadClear]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpFileUpload
  kpFileUploadDropzone (optional)
    kpFileUploadTrigger (as above)
  kpFileUploadTrigger
  kpFileUploadList
    *kpFileUploadItems
      kpFileUploadItem (repeated)
        kpFileUploadItemName
        kpFileUploadItemSize (optional)
        kpFileUploadItemRemove (optional)
  kpFileUploadClear (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(files)]: readonly File[]`: The files it holds, in order.
- `defaultFiles?: readonly File[]`: The files it starts with, when the caller does not hold `files`. Read once.
- `accept?: string | readonly string[]`: What may be taken, as a file input's `accept`: extensions (`".png"`), types (`"image/png"`) and kinds (`"image/*"`), in a list or one text with commas. Without it, anything.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether several files are held. Default `false`: a file taken is the one held.
- `maxFiles?: number`: With `multiple`, how many files it holds at most.
- `maxSize?: number`: The largest a file may be, in bytes.
- `minSize?: number`: The smallest a file may be, in bytes.
- `validate?: (file: File) => boolean`: Whether a file may be taken, asked after the checks above.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no file can be taken or removed.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, holding none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the files are submitted with the form around them.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `(filesChanged): { files: File[]; details: ChangeDetails }`: The files about to change; `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `(filesRejected): FileRejection[]`: The files that were not taken, each with its reasons.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpFileUpload]` is `KpFileUpload`. `exportAs: "kpFileUpload"`. On the element that holds the file upload's parts. `[(files)]` is the files held, in order. It draws the native file input, hidden, as its last child: what a form submits, and what the picker fills, so a trigger opens it with no dropzone in the page. `state()` is its state, for the template (`#upload="kpFileUpload"`, `upload.state().empty`). Its props are above.
- `[kpFileUploadDropzone]` is `KpFileUploadDropzone`. `exportAs: "kpFileUploadDropzone"`. Where files are dropped; a pointer's press on it opens the file picker. A group, not a control: the trigger is the keyboard's way in. `state()` is its state, for the template (`#zone="kpFileUploadDropzone"`, `zone.state().dragging`).
- `[kpFileUploadTrigger]` is `KpFileUploadTrigger`. The button that opens the file picker: the control, with or without a dropzone.
- `[kpFileUploadList]` is `KpFileUploadList`. What holds the files: a list.
- `[kpFileUploadItems]` is `KpFileUploadItems`. Structural: written `*kpFileUploadItems`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `FileUploadEntry`. `<li *kpFileUploadItems="let entry">`: once for each file, kept by the file's key.
- `[kpFileUploadItem]` is `KpFileUploadItem`. A file, on the element `*kpFileUploadItems` draws for it.
    - `entry: FileUploadEntry`: Required. The file it is, as `*kpFileUploadItems` gave it.
- `[kpFileUploadItemName]` is `KpFileUploadItemName`. Says the file's name unless the element has content of its own.
- `[kpFileUploadItemSize]` is `KpFileUploadItemSize`. Says the file's size as people read one unless the element has content of its own.
    - `locale?: string`: The language the number is written in. Default: the reader's.
- `[kpFileUploadItemRemove]` is `KpFileUploadItemRemove`. A file's button that takes it away.
- `[kpFileUploadClear]` is `KpFileUploadClear`. Takes every file away: hidden while there is none.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Files chosen to be sent. It holds the hidden file input, as its last child, and takes files pasted while focus is in it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
    - `data-empty`: Present while it holds no file.
- dropzone: Where files are dropped; a pointer's press on it opens the file picker. A group (`role="group"`), not a control: the trigger is the keyboard's way in, in it or beside it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- trigger: The button that opens the file picker: the control, which works with no dropzone in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- list: What holds the files: a list.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- item: A file.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- itemName: A file's name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- itemSize: A file's size, as people read one.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- itemRemove: A file's button that takes it away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- clear: Takes every file away: hidden while there is none.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.

### Form

```
import { KpForm } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Props:

- `errors?: FormErrors`: Errors from outside the page (a server's), by field name. A field shows its own until its value changes.
- `validationMode?: ValidationMode`: When the form's fields check their values, unless a field says otherwise. Default `"onSubmit"`.
- `(formSubmit): { values: FormValues; details: ChangeDetails }`: Every field is valid. Given this, the page is not left: the values come as an object. Without it, the form submits as a form does.
- `(clearErrors): FormErrors`: A field's value changed while it showed one of `errors`: what is left of them.

`form[kpForm]` is `KpForm`. `exportAs: "kpForm"`. On a `<form>`: its fields say what is wrong, and `(formSubmit)` gives the values once all are valid. As with Angular's own forms, the page is left only when the form has an `action`.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `root`.

### HoverCard

```
import { KpHoverCard, KpHoverCardTrigger, KpHoverCardPortal, KpHoverCardPositioner, KpHoverCardPopup, KpHoverCardArrow } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpHoverCard]`, `[kpHoverCardTrigger]`, `[kpHoverCardPortal]`, `[kpHoverCardPositioner]`, `[kpHoverCardPopup]`, `[kpHoverCardArrow]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpHoverCard
  kpHoverCardTrigger
  *kpHoverCardPortal
    kpHoverCardPositioner
      kpHoverCardPopup
        kpHoverCardArrow
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds. Default `600`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes, in milliseconds. Default `300`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the pointer and focus do not open it.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: The change with why it happened; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpHoverCard]` is `KpHoverCard`. `exportAs: "kpHoverCard"`. On any element, or on `<ng-container>` to draw none. Its props are above.
- `[kpHoverCardTrigger]` is `KpHoverCardTrigger`.
    - `delay?: number`: Its own waits, which come before the root's.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves this trigger's popup closes, in milliseconds.
- `[kpHoverCardPortal]` is `KpHoverCardPortal`. Structural: written `*kpHoverCardPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpHoverCardPositioner]` is `KpHoverCardPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpHoverCardPopup]` is `KpHoverCardPopup`.
- `[kpHoverCardArrow]` is `KpHoverCardArrow`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The link the card previews.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the card is open.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The card itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="delay | focus | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed without its usual wait, for a design that skips the motion then.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

### Input

```
import { KpInput } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Props:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed in it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: What was typed, as text, each time it changes.

`[kpInput]` is `KpInput`. `exportAs: "kpInput"`. `<input kpInput>` or `<textarea kpInput>`: it says its state, and inside a `kpField` it is the field's control. Its value is the element's own (`[value]`, `ngModel`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: A text input. Inside a field it is the field's control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the input has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the value was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the value is wrong.

### Label

```
import { KpLabel } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

`[kpLabel]` is `KpLabel`. `exportAs: "kpLabel"`. `<label kpLabel>`. Inside a `kpField` it is the field's label.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- label: A control's name. Inside a field it is the field's label, with its states.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.

### Listbox

```
import { KpListbox, KpListboxItem, KpListboxItemIndicator, KpListboxGroup, KpListboxGroupLabel } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpListbox]`, `[kpListboxItem]`, `[kpListboxItemIndicator]`, `[kpListboxGroup]`, `[kpListboxGroupLabel]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpListbox
  kpListboxGroup (optional, repeated)
    kpListboxItem (repeated)
      *kpListboxItemIndicator
    kpListboxGroupLabel
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: readonly Value[]`: The chosen values: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `defaultValue?: readonly Value[]`: The values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether more than one can be chosen: a press then adds or takes away.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no item can be chosen.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do not.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the chosen values are submitted with the form around the list.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the list belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page: each item is then given its `index`.
- `(valueChanged): { value: Value[]; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as an item is about to be chosen or taken away, with the values there would then be: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpListbox]` is `KpListbox`. `exportAs: "kpListbox"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `[kpListboxItem]` is `KpListboxItem`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What is in the listbox's value while this item is chosen.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
- `[kpListboxItemIndicator]` is `KpListboxItemIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpListboxItemIndicator`. `<span *kpListboxItemIndicator>`: in the page while its item is chosen.
- `[kpListboxGroup]` is `KpListboxGroup`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `[kpListboxGroupLabel]` is `KpListboxGroupLabel`. The name of a group.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The list. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- itemIndicator: A mark an item shows while it is chosen.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group` and `groupLabel`.

### Menu

```
import { KpMenu, KpMenuTrigger, KpMenuPortal, KpMenuPositioner, KpMenuPopup, KpMenuArrow, KpMenuItem, KpMenuLinkItem, KpMenuGroup, KpMenuGroupLabel, KpMenuSeparator, KpMenuCheckboxItem, KpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator, KpMenuRadioGroup, KpMenuRadioItem, KpMenuRadioItemIndicator, KpMenuSubmenuRoot, KpMenuSubmenuTrigger } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpMenu]`, `[kpMenuTrigger]`, `[kpMenuPortal]`, `[kpMenuPositioner]`, `[kpMenuPopup]`, `[kpMenuArrow]`, `[kpMenuItem]`, `a[kpMenuLinkItem]`, `[kpMenuGroup]`, `[kpMenuGroupLabel]`, `[kpMenuSeparator]`, `[kpMenuCheckboxItem]`, `[kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator]`, `[kpMenuRadioGroup]`, `[kpMenuRadioItem]`, `[kpMenuRadioItemIndicator]`, `[kpMenuSubmenuRoot]`, `[kpMenuSubmenuTrigger]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpMenu
  kpMenuTrigger
  *kpMenuPortal
    kpMenuPositioner
      kpMenuPopup
        kpMenuArrow
        kpMenuGroup (optional, repeated)
          kpMenuItem (repeated)
          a[kpMenuLinkItem] (repeated)
          kpMenuGroupLabel
          kpMenuCheckboxItem (repeated)
            *kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator
          kpMenuRadioGroup (repeated)
            kpMenuRadioItem (repeated)
              *kpMenuRadioItemIndicator
          kpMenuSubmenuRoot (repeated)
            *kpMenuPortal (as above)
            kpMenuSubmenuTrigger
        kpMenuSeparator (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open. Not for a submenu.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpMenu]` is `KpMenu`. `exportAs: "kpMenu"`. `kpContextMenu` in place of `kpMenu` is a menu for an area of the page, opened at the pointer: its trigger is `kpContextMenuTrigger`, its other parts the menu's. Its props are above.
- `[kpMenuTrigger]` is `KpMenuTrigger`.
- `[kpMenuPortal]` is `KpMenuPortal`. Structural: written `*kpMenuPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpMenuPositioner]` is `KpMenuPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpMenuPopup]` is `KpMenuPopup`.
- `[kpMenuArrow]` is `KpMenuArrow`.
- `[kpMenuItem]` is `KpMenuItem`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does.
- `a[kpMenuLinkItem]` is `KpMenuLinkItem`. `<a kpMenuLinkItem href="…">`: an item that is a link.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does.
- `[kpMenuGroup]` is `KpMenuGroup`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `[kpMenuGroupLabel]` is `KpMenuGroupLabel`. Names the group it is in. With no group around it, it is plain text.
- `[kpMenuSeparator]` is `KpMenuSeparator`. A line between items.
- `[kpMenuCheckboxItem]` is `KpMenuCheckboxItem`. `exportAs: "kpMenuCheckboxItem"`.
    - `[(checked)]: boolean`: Whether the item is checked, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Whether the item starts checked, when the caller does not hold `checked`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does not.
    - `(checkedChanged): { checked: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the item is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `[kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator]` is `KpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator`. `<span *kpMenuCheckboxItemIndicator>`: in the page while its item is checked.
- `[kpMenuRadioGroup]` is `KpMenuRadioGroup`. `exportAs: "kpMenuRadioGroup"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`.
    - `[(value)]: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
    - `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Value> | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
    - `(valueChanged): { value: Value; details: ChangeDetails }`: Told an item's own value, never `null`: a press chooses, and nothing takes the choice back.
- `[kpMenuRadioItem]` is `KpMenuRadioItem`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the radio group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does not.
- `[kpMenuRadioItemIndicator]` is `KpMenuRadioItemIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpMenuRadioItemIndicator`. `<span *kpMenuRadioItemIndicator>`: in the page while its item is the chosen one.
- `[kpMenuSubmenuRoot]` is `KpMenuSubmenuRoot`. `exportAs: "kpMenuSubmenuRoot"`. A menu that one of this menu's items opens. Its trigger is `kpMenuSubmenuTrigger`.
    - `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
    - `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
    - `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open. Not for a submenu.
    - `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `[kpMenuSubmenuTrigger]` is `KpMenuSubmenuTrigger`. On the item of a menu that opens the submenu around it (`kpMenuSubmenuRoot`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the menu, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss | group"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed its trigger or an item, `dismiss` when Escape closed it, `group` when focus or the pointer went from one menu of a bar to another.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `groupLabel` and `separator`.

### Menubar

```
import { KpMenubar } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Props:

- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last menu to the first. Default: they do.
- `disabled?: boolean`: No menu of the bar opens.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: A row (the default) or a column of menus. In a column a menu opens beside its trigger.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while one of its menus is open. Default `false`.

`[kpMenubar]` is `KpMenubar`. `exportAs: "kpMenubar"`. A row of menus that work as one. Each `kpMenu` inside it is one of its items.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The row of menus. A menu inside it is one of its items.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-modal`: Present when its menus hold the page while one is open.
    - `data-has-submenu-open`: Present while one of its menus is open.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its menus are in a row or a column.

### MessageScroller

```
import { KpMessageScroller, KpMessageScrollerViewport, KpMessageScrollerContent, KpMessageScrollerButton } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpMessageScroller]`, `[kpMessageScrollerViewport]`, `[kpMessageScrollerContent]`, `[kpMessageScrollerButton]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpMessageScroller
  kpMessageScrollerViewport
    kpMessageScrollerContent
  kpMessageScrollerButton
```

Props of its root:

- `initial?: "bottom" | "top"`: Where it begins: at the newest message (the default), or at the first.
