- `threshold?: number`: How near the end counts as at it, in pixels. Default: 24.
- `(atBottomChanged): { atBottom: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: It came to the end, or left it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpMessageScroller]` is `KpMessageScroller`. `exportAs: "kpMessageScroller"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpMessageScrollerViewport]` is `KpMessageScrollerViewport`.
- `[kpMessageScrollerContent]` is `KpMessageScrollerContent`. The messages: what grows as one is written.
- `[kpMessageScrollerButton]` is `KpMessageScrollerButton`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the conversation and its button.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
- viewport: What scrolls: a log, reached by the keyboard.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
- button: Goes to the newest message. Inert while that is in view.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `content`.

### Meter

```
import { KpMeter, KpMeterTrack, KpMeterIndicator, KpMeterValue, KpMeterLabel } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpMeter]`, `[kpMeterTrack]`, `[kpMeterIndicator]`, `[kpMeterValue]`, `[kpMeterLabel]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpMeter
  kpMeterTrack
    kpMeterIndicator
  kpMeterValue
  kpMeterLabel
```

Props of its root:

- `value: number`: Required. The measure, between `min` and `max`. A meter always has one.
- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `locale?: string`: The language the value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string | undefined, value: number | null) => string`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpMeter]` is `KpMeter`. `exportAs: "kpMeter"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpMeterTrack]` is `KpMeterTrack`. The whole range.
- `[kpMeterIndicator]` is `KpMeterIndicator`. The filled part: its width is the value's share of the range.
- `[kpMeterValue]` is `KpMeterValue`. Shows the written value, unless the element has content of its own.
- `[kpMeterLabel]` is `KpMeterLabel`. The meter's name.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The meter: it says the value to assistive technology.
    - `--meter-value`: The value's share of the range, a number from 0 (at `min`) to 1 (at `max`), which every part inherits: what a ring or a gauge is drawn from.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `track`, `indicator`, `value` and `label`.

### NavigationMenu

```
import { KpNavigationMenu, KpNavigationMenuList, KpNavigationMenuItem, KpNavigationMenuTrigger, KpNavigationMenuIcon, KpNavigationMenuContent, KpNavigationMenuLink, KpNavigationMenuPortal, KpNavigationMenuPositioner, KpNavigationMenuPopup, KpNavigationMenuViewport, KpNavigationMenuArrow, KpNavigationMenuBackdrop } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpNavigationMenu]`, `[kpNavigationMenuList]`, `[kpNavigationMenuItem]`, `[kpNavigationMenuTrigger]`, `[kpNavigationMenuIcon]`, `[kpNavigationMenuContent]`, `[kpNavigationMenuLink]`, `[kpNavigationMenuPortal]`, `[kpNavigationMenuPositioner]`, `[kpNavigationMenuPopup]`, `[kpNavigationMenuViewport]`, `[kpNavigationMenuArrow]`, `[kpNavigationMenuBackdrop]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpNavigationMenu
  kpNavigationMenuList
    kpNavigationMenuItem (repeated)
      kpNavigationMenuTrigger
        kpNavigationMenuIcon
      *kpNavigationMenuContent
        kpNavigationMenuLink (repeated)
      kpNavigationMenuLink (repeated, as above)
    kpNavigationMenuLink (repeated, as above)
  *kpNavigationMenuPortal
    kpNavigationMenuPositioner
      kpNavigationMenuPopup
        kpNavigationMenuViewport
        kpNavigationMenuArrow
    kpNavigationMenuBackdrop
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: Value | null`: The item whose content is shown; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Value> | null`: The item whose content it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on a trigger before its content shows, in milliseconds. Default `50`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the content goes, in milliseconds. Default `50`.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the triggers are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `(valueChanged): { value: Value | null; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as another item's content is about to show, or none: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpNavigationMenu]` is `KpNavigationMenu`. `exportAs: "kpNavigationMenu"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `[kpNavigationMenuList]` is `KpNavigationMenuList`.
- `[kpNavigationMenuItem]` is `KpNavigationMenuItem`. On an item's `<li>`. `value` tells it from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
    - `value?: unknown`: What tells this item from the others: the menu's `value` while its content is shown. An item that is given none makes its own.
- `[kpNavigationMenuTrigger]` is `KpNavigationMenuTrigger`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed, and the pointer resting on it shows nothing.
- `[kpNavigationMenuIcon]` is `KpNavigationMenuIcon`.
- `[kpNavigationMenuContent]` is `KpNavigationMenuContent`. Structural: written `*kpNavigationMenuContent`. `<div *kpNavigationMenuContent>`: an item's content, drawn in `kpNavigationMenuViewport` while it is shown.
- `[kpNavigationMenuLink]` is `KpNavigationMenuLink`.
    - `active?: boolean`: The link is the page the reader is on.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether following it closes the menu. Default: it does.
- `[kpNavigationMenuPortal]` is `KpNavigationMenuPortal`. Structural: written `*kpNavigationMenuPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpNavigationMenuPositioner]` is `KpNavigationMenuPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpNavigationMenuPopup]` is `KpNavigationMenuPopup`.
- `[kpNavigationMenuViewport]` is `KpNavigationMenuViewport`. Where the contents are drawn, inside the popup.
- `[kpNavigationMenuArrow]` is `KpNavigationMenuArrow`.
- `[kpNavigationMenuBackdrop]` is `KpNavigationMenuBackdrop`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The navigation.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
    - `data-open`: Present while an item's content is shown.
    - `data-nested`: Present on a navigation menu inside another's content: a submenu of it.
- list: The row of items.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
    - `data-open`: Present while an item's content is shown.
- trigger: The button that shows an item's content.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- icon: A mark on a trigger that shows whether its content is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
- content: What an item shows. It is drawn in the viewport every item shares.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down"`: Which way it came from: the item before it, or after; `up` and `down` when the list is a column.
- link: A link, in the list or in an item's content.
    - `data-active`: Present on the link of the page the reader is on.
- positioner: Places the popup against the open item's trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-instant`: Present while it should move at once: as it is first drawn, and while the window is resized.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--positioner-height`: The open content's height.
- popup: The panel every item's content is shown in.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--popup-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--popup-height`: The open content's height.
- arrow: An element that points at the open item's trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- backdrop: An element behind the popup, for a design that dims the page.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `item` and `viewport`.

### NumberField

```
import { KpNumberField, KpNumberFieldGroup, KpNumberFieldInput, KpNumberFieldIncrement, KpNumberFieldDecrement, KpNumberFieldScrubArea, KpNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpNumberField]`, `[kpNumberFieldGroup]`, `[kpNumberFieldInput]`, `[kpNumberFieldIncrement]`, `[kpNumberFieldDecrement]`, `[kpNumberFieldScrubArea]`, `[kpNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpNumberField
  kpNumberFieldGroup
    kpNumberFieldInput
    kpNumberFieldIncrement
    kpNumberFieldDecrement
  kpNumberFieldScrubArea
    *kpNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: number | null`: The number; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: number | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `min?: number`: The least the number may be.
- `max?: number`: The most the number may be.
- `step?: number`: What the buttons and the arrows move by. Default 1.
- `smallStep?: number`: With Alt held. Default 0.1.
- `largeStep?: number`: With Shift held. Default 10.
- `snapOnStep?: boolean`: A step lands on a multiple of the step, counted from `min`.
- `allowWheelScrub?: boolean`: The wheel steps it while the pointer is over the input and focus is in it.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the number is written.
- `locale?: string`: The language it is written in; the page's by default.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the number is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `kpId?: string`: What its input's id is made from: the input is `<id>-input`, which a `<label for>` names. Inside a `Field`, the input takes the field's id instead. An `id` given to the input itself wins over both.
- `(valueChanged): { value: number | null; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the number is about to change, typed or stepped: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(valueCommitted): { value: number | null; details: ChangeDetails }`: A change that is done: focus left the input, a key or a button stepped it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpNumberField]` is `KpNumberField`. `exportAs: "kpNumberField"`. On the element that holds the field's parts. `[(value)]` is the number, `null` for none. With a name, it draws the hidden input a form reads. Its props are above.
- `[kpNumberFieldGroup]` is `KpNumberFieldGroup`.
- `[kpNumberFieldInput]` is `KpNumberFieldInput`.
- `[kpNumberFieldIncrement]` is `KpNumberFieldIncrement`.
- `[kpNumberFieldDecrement]` is `KpNumberFieldDecrement`.
- `[kpNumberFieldScrubArea]` is `KpNumberFieldScrubArea`. On the element that is pressed and dragged to change the number: the field's label, as a rule.
    - `direction?: "horizontal" | "vertical"`: The way the pointer is dragged: `"horizontal"`, where right is more, or `"vertical"`, where up is more. Default `"horizontal"`.
    - `pixelSensitivity?: number`: How many pixels the pointer moves before the number changes. Default 2.
    - `teleportDistance?: number`: How far past the area's edges the drawn cursor goes before it comes back in at the other side. Default: the edges of the window.
- `[kpNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor]` is `KpNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor`. Structural: written `*kpNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor`. `<span *kpNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor>`: drawn in place of the pointer while it is locked for a drag, at the end of the page.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the number field's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- group: What holds the input and its buttons, as one control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- input: The text input: it takes what its locale writes a number with. It is named `<root id>-input`, or in a `Field` by the field's id; an `id` given to it is kept, so a `<label for>` and the buttons' `aria-controls` name it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- increment: A button that steps the number up. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- decrement: A button that steps the number down. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubArea: An area that is pressed and dragged to change the number: the field's label, as a rule. It takes `direction`, `pixelSensitivity` and `teleportDistance`. A mouse's pointer is locked for the drag where the browser has that (not in Safari); a finger drags as it is.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubAreaCursor: What is drawn in place of the pointer while it is locked for a drag: in the page only then, at the end of `<body>`, placed by the component.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.

### Otp

```
import { KpOtp, KpOtpInput, KpOtpGroup, KpOtpSlot, KpOtpSeparator, KpOtpCaret } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpOtp]`, `input[kpOtpInput]`, `[kpOtpGroup]`, `[kpOtpSlot]`, `[kpOtpSeparator]`, `[kpOtpCaret]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpOtp
  input[kpOtpInput]
  kpOtpGroup (repeated)
    kpOtpSlot (repeated)
      *kpOtpCaret
  kpOtpSeparator (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `length?: number`: How many characters the code has. Default: 6.
- `[(value)]: string`: The characters typed so far, when the caller holds them.
- `defaultValue?: string`: The characters it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `validationType?: OtpValidation`: What a character may be: a digit (`numeric`), a letter (`alpha`, `a` to `z` either case), either (`alphanumeric`), or anything but white space (`none`: no rule beyond that). It also says which keyboard a phone shows: the digits' for `numeric`, letters' otherwise. Default: `numeric`, on purpose: a one-time code is digits, and its keyboard is then the one to type them on. `alphabetic` and `text` are older spellings of `alpha` and `none`, still read.
- `pattern?: string`: What else a character may be: a regular expression, as text, that one character must match whole (`"[A-F0-9]"`), in place of `validationType`'s rule. Text, as an attribute can only be, so it is given the same way on every framework and on a custom element. With a pattern, `validationType` only says the keyboard, and defaults to `none`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a field, an empty code is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the code is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the input belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `kpId?: string`: The id of its input, not of the root, unless the input is given its own: a `<label for>` names it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the characters are about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `(valueCompleted): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Every character is in: the moment to send the code, with the change's details.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpOtp]` is `KpOtp`. `exportAs: "kpOtp"`. Its props are above.
- `input[kpOtpInput]` is `KpOtpInput`. `<input kpOtpInput>`: the one input the code is typed in.
- `[kpOtpGroup]` is `KpOtpGroup`. Cells that are drawn together.
- `[kpOtpSlot]` is `KpOtpSlot`. One cell. It writes its character before whatever is inside it (a caret), and leaves that alone.
    - `index: number`: Required. Which character of the code it shows, from 0.
- `[kpOtpSeparator]` is `KpOtpSeparator`. A mark between groups of cells.
- `[kpOtpCaret]` is `KpOtpCaret`. Structural: written `*kpOtpCaret`. `<div *kpOtpCaret>`: in its cell while the cell is the active one and empty.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The code: the input and its cells.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present when the code has a character in it.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-complete`: Present when every character is in.
- input: The one input the code is typed in. A design lays it over the cells, unseen. It is named by the root's `id`; an `id` given to it is kept, so a `<label for>` names it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- slot: One cell of the code.
    - `data-index`: The cell's place, from 0.
    - `data-active`: Present on the cell the next character goes in, or that is selected.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present when the cell has its character.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-complete`: Present when every character is in.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `separator` and `caret`.

### Pagination

```
import { KpPagination, KpPaginationItems, KpPaginationItem, KpPaginationEllipsis, KpPaginationPrevious, KpPaginationNext } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpPagination]`, `[kpPaginationItems]`, `[kpPaginationItem]`, `[kpPaginationEllipsis]`, `[kpPaginationPrevious]`, `[kpPaginationNext]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpPagination
  *kpPaginationItems
    kpPaginationItem (repeated)
    kpPaginationEllipsis (repeated)
  kpPaginationPrevious
  kpPaginationNext
```

Props of its root:

- `[(page)]: number`: The page shown, from 1.
- `defaultPage?: number`: The page it starts at, when the caller does not hold `page`. Read once. Default `1`.
- `count: number`: Required. How many items there are in all.
- `pageSize?: number`: How many items a page holds. Default 10.
- `siblingCount?: number`: How many pages are listed each side of the one shown. Default 1.
- `boundaryCount?: number`: How many pages are always listed at each end. Default 1.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no page can be gone to.
- `(pageChanged): { page: number; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as another page is about to be shown: `details.cancel()` keeps the page as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpPagination]` is `KpPagination`. `exportAs: "kpPagination"`. On a `<nav>`. `[(page)]` is the page shown, from 1. Its props are above.
- `[kpPaginationItems]` is `KpPaginationItems`. Structural: written `*kpPaginationItems`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `PaginationEntry`. `<ng-container *kpPaginationItems="let entry">`: once for each piece of the row, a page or the mark for pages left out.
- `[kpPaginationItem]` is `KpPaginationItem`.
    - `page: number`: Required. The page it goes to, from 1.
- `[kpPaginationEllipsis]` is `KpPaginationEllipsis`. The mark for pages left out of the row.
- `[kpPaginationPrevious]` is `KpPaginationPrevious`.
- `[kpPaginationNext]` is `KpPaginationNext`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The pages of a list, as a navigation.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: A page: pressed, it is the one shown.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the page that is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- previous: Goes to the page before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes to the page after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `ellipsis`.

### PasswordInput

```
import { KpPasswordInput, KpPasswordInputInput, KpPasswordInputToggle, KpPasswordInputIndicator } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpPasswordInput]`, `[kpPasswordInputInput]`, `[kpPasswordInputToggle]`, `[kpPasswordInputIndicator]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpPasswordInput
  kpPasswordInputInput
  kpPasswordInputToggle
    kpPasswordInputIndicator (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(visible)]: boolean`: Whether the password can be read, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultVisible?: boolean`: Read once. Default `false`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed in it.
- `toggleLabels?: { show?: string | undefined; hide?: string | undefined }`: What the toggle is called, for assistive technology: `show` while the password is hidden, `hide` while it is shown. Default: `"Show password"` and `"Hide password"`. An `aria-label` on the toggle itself wins over both.
- `(visibleChanged): { visible: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: About to be shown or hidden; `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(valueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: What was typed, as text, each time it changes.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpPasswordInput]` is `KpPasswordInput`. `exportAs: "kpPasswordInput"`. On the element that holds the password's parts. `[(visible)]` is whether the password can be read. Its value is the input's own (`[value]`, `ngModel`). `state()` is its state, for the template (`#password="kpPasswordInput"`). Its props are above.
- `[kpPasswordInputInput]` is `KpPasswordInputInput`. `<input kpPasswordInputInput>`: a password, or text while it is shown.
- `[kpPasswordInputToggle]` is `KpPasswordInputToggle`. `exportAs: "kpPasswordInputToggle"`. Shows the password, and hides it again: named by the root's `toggleLabels`, or by its own `aria-label`. `state()` is its state, for the template (`#toggle="kpPasswordInputToggle"`).
- `[kpPasswordInputIndicator]` is `KpPasswordInputIndicator`. `exportAs: "kpPasswordInputIndicator"`. What draws which of the two it is: it says the state only. `state()` is that state, for the template: `<span kpPasswordInputIndicator #eye="kpPasswordInputIndicator">`, then `@if (eye.state().visible) { … }`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A password that can be shown while it is typed.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: The `<input>`: a password, or text while it is shown. In a `Field` it is the field's control.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: Present once its text differs from what it began with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: Present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the value was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the value is wrong.
- toggle: Shows the password, and hides it again. Focus and the caret stay in the input. It is named "Show password" while the password is hidden and "Hide password" while it is shown, and that name is how its state is told: it is a plain button, with no `aria-pressed`. The root's `toggleLabels` (`{ show, hide }`) words them in the page's language, and an `aria-label` given to the toggle wins over both.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: An element hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden`) that holds what the design draws to say which of the two it is, an eye open or struck, by its `data-visible`. It has no content of its own.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Popover

```
import { KpPopover, KpPopoverTrigger, KpPopoverPortal, KpPopoverBackdrop, KpPopoverPositioner, KpPopoverPopup, KpPopoverArrow, KpPopoverTitle, KpPopoverDescription, KpPopoverClose } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpPopover]`, `[kpPopoverTrigger]`, `[kpPopoverPortal]`, `[kpPopoverBackdrop]`, `[kpPopoverPositioner]`, `[kpPopoverPopup]`, `[kpPopoverArrow]`, `[kpPopoverTitle]`, `[kpPopoverDescription]`, `[kpPopoverClose]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpPopover
  kpPopoverTrigger
  *kpPopoverPortal
    kpPopoverBackdrop
    kpPopoverPositioner
      kpPopoverPopup
        kpPopoverTitle
        kpPopoverDescription
        kpPopoverClose
        kpPopoverArrow
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal?: boolean | "trap-focus"`: What the page behind it may do while it is open. `false` (the default): everything. `true`: nothing, the page is inert and does not scroll, and Tab stays inside the popover. `"trap-focus"`: Tab stays inside the popover, and the page can still be pressed and scrolled. A popover the pointer opened holds nothing until it is pressed. Read as it opens.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpPopover]` is `KpPopover`. `exportAs: "kpPopover"`. Holds the popover: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `[kpPopoverTrigger]` is `KpPopoverTrigger`.
    - `openOnHover?: boolean`: Whether the pointer resting on the trigger opens the popover too. A press and the keyboard still open it, and a press on one the pointer opened keeps it open. Default `false`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popover opens, in milliseconds. Default 300.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves a popover it opened closes, in milliseconds. Default 0.
- `[kpPopoverPortal]` is `KpPopoverPortal`. Structural: written `*kpPopoverPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpPopoverBackdrop]` is `KpPopoverBackdrop`.
- `[kpPopoverPositioner]` is `KpPopoverPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kpPopoverPopup]` is `KpPopoverPopup`.
- `[kpPopoverArrow]` is `KpPopoverArrow`.
- `[kpPopoverTitle]` is `KpPopoverTitle`. The heading that names the popover.
- `[kpPopoverDescription]` is `KpPopoverDescription`. The text that describes the popover.
- `[kpPopoverClose]` is `KpPopoverClose`. A button that closes the popover.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while the popover a press on this trigger opened is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
- backdrop: A layer over the page behind the popover.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed the trigger, `dismiss` when Escape closed it.
    - `--popup-width`: Its width: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old width and then the new one, for a transition between them.
    - `--popup-height`: Its height: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old height and then the new one, for a transition between them.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `title`, `description` and `close`.

### Progress

```
import { KpProgress, KpProgressTrack, KpProgressIndicator, KpProgressValue, KpProgressLabel } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpProgress]`, `[kpProgressTrack]`, `[kpProgressIndicator]`, `[kpProgressValue]`, `[kpProgressLabel]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpProgress
  kpProgressTrack
    kpProgressIndicator
  kpProgressValue
  kpProgressLabel
```

Props of its root:

- `value: number | null`: Required. The value. For a progress bar, `null` is "under way, how far is not known".
- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `locale?: string`: The language the value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string | undefined, value: number | null) => string`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpProgress]` is `KpProgress`. `exportAs: "kpProgress"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpProgressTrack]` is `KpProgressTrack`.
- `[kpProgressIndicator]` is `KpProgressIndicator`.
- `[kpProgressValue]` is `KpProgressValue`. Shows the written value, unless the element has content of its own.
- `[kpProgressLabel]` is `KpProgressLabel`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The progress bar: it says the value to assistive technology.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
    - `--progress-value`: The value's share of the range, a number from 0 (at `min`) to 1 (at `max`), which every part inherits: what a ring or a gauge is drawn from. Absent while the value is not known.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- indicator: The filled part: its width is the value's share of the range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- label: The bar's name.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.

### QrCode

```
import { KpQrCode, KpQrCodeFrame, KpQrCodePattern } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpQrCode]`, `[kpQrCodeFrame]`, `[kpQrCodePattern]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpQrCode
  kpQrCodeFrame
    kpQrCodePattern
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: string`: What the code says: a link, a text.
- `correction?: QrCorrection`: How much of it may be lost and still be read. Default: `"M"`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpQrCode]` is `KpQrCode`. `exportAs: "kpQrCode"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpQrCodeFrame]` is `KpQrCodeFrame`. `<svg kpQrCodeFrame>`: the drawing.
- `[kpQrCodePattern]` is `KpQrCodePattern`. `<svg:path kpQrCodePattern>`: the dark modules.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the code.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the value is longer than a code holds.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `frame` and `pattern`.

### RadioGroup

```
import { KpRadioGroup, KpRadioGroupItem, KpRadioGroupIndicator } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpRadioGroup]`, `[kpRadioGroupItem]`, `[kpRadioGroupIndicator]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpRadioGroup
  kpRadioGroupItem (repeated)
    *kpRadioGroupIndicator
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Value> | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, choosing none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the chosen value is submitted with the form around the group.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: Value | null; details: ChangeDetails }`: The change with why it happened; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpRadioGroup]` is `KpRadioGroup`. `exportAs: "kpRadioGroup"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `[kpRadioGroupItem]` is `KpRadioGroupItem`. On an item's element. It draws the hidden native radio inside it, which a form and a label reach.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen.
    - `kpId?: string`: The id of the item's native radio, unique in the page: a `<label for>` names it.
- `[kpRadioGroupIndicator]` is `KpRadioGroupIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpRadioGroupIndicator`. `<span *kpRadioGroupIndicator>`: in the page while its item is the chosen one.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items: one of them is chosen at most.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- item: One choice. It holds a hidden native radio, which a form and a label reach: the item's `id` (`kpId` on Angular, `kui-id` on a custom element) is the radio's, which a `<label for>` names.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while its item is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Rating

```
import { KpRating, KpRatingItems, KpRatingItem } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpRating]`, `[kpRatingItems]`, `[kpRatingItem]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpRating
  *kpRatingItems
    kpRatingItem (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: number`: How much is given, from 0 (none) to `count`; a half where `allowHalf` is set.
- `defaultValue?: number`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once. Default `0`.
- `count?: number`: How many items there are. Default 5.
- `allowHalf?: boolean`: Whether half an item can be given: by the half of it a pointer is over, and by the arrows.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, giving none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it; none is submitted as empty.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `(valueChanged): { value: number; details: ChangeDetails }`: The change with why it happened; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.
- `(hoverChanged): number | null`: The value the pointer is over, and `null` as it leaves: nothing is chosen by it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpRating]` is `KpRating`. `exportAs: "kpRating"`. On the element that holds the items. `[(value)]` is how much is given, from 0 to `count`. It draws the hidden input a form reads, as its last child. Its props are above.
- `[kpRatingItems]` is `KpRatingItems`. Structural: written `*kpRatingItems`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `number`. `<ng-container *kpRatingItems="let place">`: once for each item, from 1 to `count`.
- `[kpRatingItem]` is `KpRatingItem`. `exportAs: "kpRatingItem"`. One item, at its `place`. `state()` is its state, for the template: `#star="kpRatingItem"`, then `@if (star.state().half) { … }`.
    - `place: number`: Required. Its place among the items, from 1.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The items, as one choice: a radio group. It holds the hidden input a form reads.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a value is needed.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while a pointer is over an item.
- item: One item (a star): pressed, the value is its place, or half of it.
    - `data-checked`: Present on the item that holds the value.
    - `data-filled`: Present on every item up to the value drawn: the one a pointer is over, or the one held.
    - `data-half`: Present on the item the value drawn fills by half, which has `data-filled` too. No variable says how much is filled: a design draws the half, an element of its own in the item (a filled star over an empty one) clipped to its first half: `[data-half] .star-fill { clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0) }`, `inset(0 0 0 50%)` where the text runs right to left.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a value is needed.

### Resizable

```
import { KpResizableGroup, KpResizablePanel, KpResizableHandle } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpResizableGroup]`, `[kpResizablePanel]`, `[kpResizableHandle]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpResizableGroup
  kpResizablePanel (repeated)
  kpResizableHandle (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the panels are side by side (the default) or one over the other.
- `keyboardStep?: number`: How far an arrow key moves a handle, in hundredths of the group. Default: 10.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the handles cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.
- `(sizesChanged): { sizes: number[]; details: ChangeDetails }`: Each panel's share as the panels are resized, with why.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpResizableGroup]` is `KpResizableGroup`. `exportAs: "kpResizableGroup"`. Its props are above.
- `[kpResizablePanel]` is `KpResizablePanel`.
    - `defaultSize?: number`: Its share to begin with, in hundredths of the group. Either every panel gives one or none does (they are then equal).
    - `minSize?: number`: The least it can be made. Default: 0.
    - `maxSize?: number`: The most it can be made. Default: 100.
- `[kpResizableHandle]` is `KpResizableHandle`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this handle: it cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- group: The panels and the bars between them. A design lays it out as a flex box: `display: flex`, and `flex-direction: column` when it is vertical. A group in a panel that is a flex box itself takes `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, or what it holds widens the panel.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: One panel. It carries its share of the group, written as its `flex` with `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, so what it holds cannot keep it past its share. Its `overflow` is the design's.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `--panel-size`: The panel's share, in hundredths of the group.
- handle: The bar between two panels: dragged, or moved with the arrows. A design gives it its thickness and `flex-shrink: 0`, so the panels do not squeeze it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while the bar is dragged.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ScrollArea

```
import { KpScrollArea, KpScrollAreaViewport, KpScrollAreaContent, KpScrollAreaScrollbar, KpScrollAreaThumb, KpScrollAreaCorner } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpScrollArea]`, `[kpScrollAreaViewport]`, `[kpScrollAreaContent]`, `[kpScrollAreaScrollbar]`, `[kpScrollAreaThumb]`, `[kpScrollAreaCorner]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpScrollArea
  kpScrollAreaViewport
    kpScrollAreaContent (optional)
    *kpScrollAreaScrollbar (repeated, as above)
  *kpScrollAreaScrollbar (repeated)
    kpScrollAreaThumb
  *kpScrollAreaCorner
```

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpScrollArea]` is `KpScrollArea`. `exportAs: "kpScrollArea"`.
- `[kpScrollAreaViewport]` is `KpScrollAreaViewport`.
- `[kpScrollAreaContent]` is `KpScrollAreaContent`.
- `[kpScrollAreaScrollbar]` is `KpScrollAreaScrollbar`. Structural: written `*kpScrollAreaScrollbar`. `<div *kpScrollAreaScrollbar="'horizontal'">`: in the page while there is something to scroll its way (`vertical` when no orientation is given).
    - `*kpScrollAreaScrollbar: Orientation | ""`: The directive's own value: `*kpScrollAreaScrollbar="…"`. Which way it scrolls: `'horizontal'`, or `'vertical'` when none is given.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Written after the directive's value: `*kpScrollAreaScrollbar="…; keepMounted: …"`. In the page even while there is nothing to scroll its way.
- `[kpScrollAreaThumb]` is `KpScrollAreaThumb`.
- `[kpScrollAreaCorner]` is `KpScrollAreaCorner`. Structural: written `*kpScrollAreaCorner`. `<div *kpScrollAreaCorner>`: in the page while both scrollbars are.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The area. It holds the viewport and the scrollbars, which the library places against it: a design gives a scrollbar its thickness and draws it, and places nothing.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-width`: The width of the corner: the vertical scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-height`: The height of the corner: the horizontal scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
- viewport: The element that scrolls.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-x-start`: How far the view is from the start of a line, to fade that edge by: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-x-end`: How far the view is from the end of a line: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-y-start`: How far the view is from the top: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-y-end`: How far the view is from the bottom: `0px` at it.
- content: A box around what is scrolled, as wide as what it holds. Not needed to measure: the viewport's children are watched as they are. For content whose own box does not grow with what is in it (a block holding a wider table, or bare text).
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
- scrollbar: A scrollbar's track, placed along its edge of the area. In the page while there is something to scroll its way.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-height`: A vertical thumb's height.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-width`: A horizontal thumb's width.
- thumb: The part of a scrollbar that shows where the view is, and can be dragged. As long as its scrollbar's variable says.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.

This part writes no state attribute or CSS variable of its own: `corner`.

### Select

```
import { KpSelect, KpSelectTrigger, KpSelectValue, KpSelectPortal, KpSelectBackdrop, KpSelectPositioner, KpSelectPopup, KpSelectList, KpSelectScrollUpArrow, KpSelectScrollDownArrow, KpSelectGroup, KpSelectGroupLabel, KpSelectSeparator, KpSelectItem, KpSelectItemText, KpSelectItemIndicator, KpSelectInput } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpSelect]`, `[kpSelectTrigger]`, `[kpSelectValue]`, `[kpSelectPortal]`, `[kpSelectBackdrop]`, `[kpSelectPositioner]`, `[kpSelectPopup]`, `[kpSelectList]`, `[kpSelectScrollUpArrow]`, `[kpSelectScrollDownArrow]`, `[kpSelectGroup]`, `[kpSelectGroupLabel]`, `[kpSelectSeparator]`, `[kpSelectItem]`, `[kpSelectItemText]`, `[kpSelectItemIndicator]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpSelect
  kpSelectTrigger
    *kpSelectValue (or kpSelectValue as an attribute)
  *kpSelectPortal
    kpSelectBackdrop (optional)
    kpSelectPositioner
      kpSelectPopup
        *kpSelectScrollUpArrow
        kpSelectList (optional)
          kpSelectGroup (optional, repeated)
            kpSelectGroupLabel
            kpSelectItem (repeated)
              kpSelectItemText
              *kpSelectItemIndicator
          kpSelectSeparator (repeated)
        *kpSelectScrollDownArrow
  input[kpSelectInput] (Angular only)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: (Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null)`: With `[multiple]="true"`, the chosen values.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null>`: The value it starts with (with `multiple`, the values), when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: the list still opens, and nothing is chosen.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: ItemLabels<Value>`: The values' labels: a list of values with their labels, or the labels by value.
- `multiple?: Multiple`: Several values: `value` and `valueChanged` then hold a list. Bound to `true` (`[multiple]="true"`), it types them so. The bare attribute, or a bound boolean, works the same, and then `value` takes either and `valueChanged` is typed as one value: Angular's compiler gives a type parameter it cannot infer `any`, so only a literal `true` says it.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page: each item is then given its `index`.
- `presentation?: Presentation`: How the list opens: `"sheet"` from the bottom edge, modal, with a backdrop; `"auto"` a sheet on a narrow touch screen. Default `"popup"`.
- `sheetBelow?: number`: With `presentation="auto"`: the viewport's width under which a coarse pointer opens a sheet. Default 640.
- `itemToStringLabel?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the trigger shows for one, and what typing matches.
- `itemToStringValue?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the form is sent for one.
- `(valueChanged): { value: true extends Multiple ? (false extends Multiple ? Value | null : Value[]) : Value | null details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as a value is about to be chosen (with `multiple`, added or taken away, with the values there would then be): `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpSelect]` is `KpSelect`. `exportAs: "kpSelect"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown, Multiple extends boolean = false>`. Holds the select: its value and whether the list is open. Its props are above.
- `[kpSelectTrigger]` is `KpSelectTrigger`. `<button kpSelectTrigger>`. A select with a name, its own or its field's, submits its value through a hidden input drawn right after the trigger, where the other adapters draw it after the root's content.
- `[kpSelectValue]` is `KpSelectValue`. Structural or not: written `*kpSelectValue`, or as an attribute, `kpSelectValue`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `SelectShown`. `<span kpSelectValue>` shows the chosen value's label, or `placeholder` while nothing is chosen; with `multiple`, the chosen labels with commas between. An element with content of its own says that instead. `<span *kpSelectValue="let shown">` draws its own content instead, with what is chosen: `shown.value` and `shown.label`, with `multiple` `shown.values` and `shown.labels`, in the items' order.
    - `placeholder?: string`: Shown while nothing is chosen.
- `[kpSelectPortal]` is `KpSelectPortal`. Structural: written `*kpSelectPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kpSelectBackdrop]` is `KpSelectBackdrop`. `<div kpSelectBackdrop>`, in the portal: what lies over the page behind the list.
- `[kpSelectPositioner]` is `KpSelectPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
    - `alignItemWithTrigger?: boolean`: The list opens over its trigger, the chosen item's text on the trigger's own, where there is room and unless a finger opened it. While it lies there the page's scroll is held (its scrollbar's room kept), and a scroll of a box around the trigger closes the list (`"ancestor-scroll"`), as a change of the window's size does (`"window-resize"`).
- `[kpSelectPopup]` is `KpSelectPopup`.
- `[kpSelectList]` is `KpSelectList`. The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup also holds scroll arrows.
- `[kpSelectScrollUpArrow]` is `KpSelectScrollUpArrow`. Structural: written `*kpSelectScrollUpArrow`. `<div *kpSelectScrollUpArrow>`: in the page while there is more of the list above. It scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
- `[kpSelectScrollDownArrow]` is `KpSelectScrollDownArrow`. Structural: written `*kpSelectScrollDownArrow`. `<div *kpSelectScrollDownArrow>`: in the page while there is more of the list below.
- `[kpSelectGroup]` is `KpSelectGroup`. Items that belong together, named by their `kpSelectGroupLabel`.
- `[kpSelectGroupLabel]` is `KpSelectGroupLabel`. Names the group it is in. With no group around it, it is plain text.
- `[kpSelectSeparator]` is `KpSelectSeparator`. A line between groups.
- `[kpSelectItem]` is `KpSelectItem`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the select's value is while this item is chosen.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typeahead matches and the trigger shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
- `[kpSelectItemText]` is `KpSelectItemText`. The item's name: what the trigger shows once it is chosen.
- `[kpSelectItemIndicator]` is `KpSelectItemIndicator`. Structural: written `*kpSelectItemIndicator`. `<span *kpSelectItemIndicator>`: in the page while its item is the chosen one.
- `input[kpSelectInput]` is `KpSelectInput`. `<input kpSelectInput>`: submits the value with the form around it. A page that writes one keeps it, and the trigger then draws none. Angular only.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that shows the value and opens the list.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- value: The chosen value's label, or the placeholder. With several values, their labels with commas between.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the list: a press on it closes the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
- positioner: Places the list against the trigger. It carries the geometry. As a sheet it is not placed, and carries none.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- scrollUpArrow: In the page while there is more of the list above: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- scrollDownArrow: In the page while there is more of the list below: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- popup: The list of items. As a sheet, a design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: As a sheet, once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item, or on each of several.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

These parts write no state attribute or CSS variable of their own: `group`, `groupLabel`, `separator`, `list`, `itemText` and `itemIndicator`.

### Separator

```
import { KpSeparator } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Props:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the line lies across (the default) or stands upright: what a screen reader is told.

`[kpSeparator]` is `KpSeparator`. `exportAs: "kpSeparator"`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The line.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the line runs.

### Slider

```
import { KpSlider, KpSliderValue, KpSliderControl, KpSliderTrack, KpSliderIndicator, KpSliderThumb } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kpSlider]`, `[kpSliderValue]`, `[kpSliderControl]`, `[kpSliderTrack]`, `[kpSliderIndicator]`, `[kpSliderThumb]`.

Anatomy:

```
kpSlider
  kpSliderValue
  kpSliderControl
    kpSliderTrack
      kpSliderIndicator
      kpSliderThumb (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: Value`: A number for one thumb, a list for a range: what is told back is the same kind.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Value>`: Read once. Default `min`.
- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `step?: number`: Default 1.
- `largeStep?: number`: What Page Up, Page Down and an arrow with Shift move by. Default 10.
- `minStepsBetweenValues?: number`: How many steps two thumbs of a range stay apart. Default 0.
- `thumbAlignment?: "center" | "edge" | "edge-client-only"`: `"edge"` keeps a thumb inside the control at the ends of its range. Default `"center"`.
- `orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical"`: Whether the track lies across (the default) or stands upright: the arrows that move a thumb follow.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable; its value is still submitted.
- `name?: string`: With a name, each thumb's value is submitted with the form around the slider.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How a value is written.
- `locale?: string`: The language a value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string, value: number, index: number) => string`: What assistive technology reads for a thumb, when the written value is not enough.
- `(valueChanged): { value: SliderTold<Value>; details: SliderChangeDetails }`: Each step of a drag and each key, with why; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.
- `(valueCommitted): { value: SliderTold<Value>; details: SliderChangeDetails }`: When the pointer lets go, and after each key.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kpSlider]` is `KpSlider`. `exportAs: "kpSlider"`. Generic: `<Value extends SliderValue = SliderValue>`. Its props are above.
- `[kpSliderValue]` is `KpSliderValue`. Shows the written value, unless the element has content of its own.
- `[kpSliderControl]` is `KpSliderControl`.
- `[kpSliderTrack]` is `KpSliderTrack`.
- `[kpSliderIndicator]` is `KpSliderIndicator`.
- `[kpSliderThumb]` is `KpSliderThumb`. On a thumb's element. It draws the hidden input inside it, which a form reads.
    - `index?: number`: Which value of a range the thumb is, from 0. A thumb that is given none takes its place among the slider's thumbs, in the order they are written.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the slider's parts.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- control: What a pointer presses and drags on. It holds the track and the thumbs.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The filled part: up to the thumb, or from the first thumb to the last. Its place and length are written on it inline, and a design does not set these: `position: relative`, `inset-inline-start` and `width`, with `height: inherit` (on a vertical slider, `position: absolute`, `bottom` and `height`, with `width: inherit`).
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `--start-position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the filled part starts, or with one thumb where it ends.
    - `--relative-size`: With thumbs that stay inside the control and a range: the filled part's length.
- thumb: What is dragged, and what the keyboard moves: a slider to assistive technology. Its place on the track is written on it inline, and a design does not set these: `position: absolute`, `inset-inline-start` at its value's place and `top: 50%` (on a vertical slider, `bottom` and `left: 50%`), and a `translate` that centres it there (with `thumbAlignment: "edge"`, one that keeps it inside).
